item.title: Joao Cancelo emerges as Alejandro Balde’s biggest supporter at Barcelona
item.description: Joao Cancelo emerges as Alejandro Balde’s biggest supporter at Barcelona Joao Cancelo has emerged as one of Alejandro Balde’s strongest supporters within the Barcelona dressing room, offering encouragement and advice as the defender struggles to establish himself under Hansi Flick. According to Mundo Deportivo , the Portuguese full-back has even defended his teammate in conversations with the German manager, while showing concern among senior players over Balde’s situation. The development comes amid uncertainty surrounding Balde’s Barcelona future. As previously reported, the academy graduate is increasingly open to leaving in January after struggling to secure regular playing time. In fact, despite Barcelona’s defensive injury problems, he has managed just 116 minutes across four appearances, raising questions about his standing in Flick’s plans. Cancelo takes Alejandro Balde under his wing Cancelo has emerged as Balde’s biggest supporter. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Cancelo’s support is, in fact, an interesting development given Balde’s initial reaction to his arrival at Barcelona. As per the outlet, the Spaniard struggled to understand the decision to sign another left-back, particularly as he was expected to be Flick’s first choice. As it turns out, however, their relationship has evolved, with the experienced Portuguese defender now regularly encouraging Balde, offering advice and reassuring him during a difficult period. It has even been suggested that Cancelo has also spoken to Flick in his teammate’s defence on at least one occasion. Another Barcelona senior player questions Flick As per the outlet, Cancelo is not the only senior figure concerned about how Flick has handled Balde, as another influential Barcelona player, who enjoys direct communication with the manager, also questioned one of his training decisions. Balde is likely to leave Barcelona in January. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The incident involved Flick changing Balde’s position during a training match. The teammate reportedly challenged the decision, questioning how the defender could demonstrate his abilities when he was not being trained in his natural position. What happens now? Notably, the situation adds to Balde’s increasingly difficult relationship with his role at Barcelona. Having spent most of his development at the club since joining the academy, he is now facing uncertainty over his long-term prospects. Now, with January approaching, the support of senior dressing-room figures could prove important, although unless his opportunities improve, Balde may still consider leaving to secure the regular football he wants.

item.title: INTERVIEW: Ex-Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela on why Jürgen Klopp is "a good fit" for Germany
item.description: INTERVIEW: Ex-Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela on why Jürgen Klopp is "a good fit" for Germany MÜNCHEN ( Bulinews ): Ex-Borussia Dortmund star Patrick Owomoyela is confident Jürgen Klopp is the right man who can restore the German national team to it's former glory. “He is able to change the important things in a short matter of time, and that’s what makes him a good fit," Owomoyela said at a media round in Munich attended by Bulinews.com . “I wish he could have the Germany guys every day [to practice] but that’s not the case. As I said, he’s able to create an instant impact and a clear vision of what to do. “Now more than before, his reputation helps players believe what he is saying. All of that is a good fit for a coach with less time but can make things happen. “It’s just about finding the right people. He used a lot of players [in his first international period] and that will be the case going forward too," the Hamburg native added. Having played under Klopp at Dortmund for five seasons between 2008 and 2013, Owomoyela gave some fascinating insights into what the 59-year-old demands from his squad. “He was a coach who pushed for hard work but have fun while doing it. He always had fun it seemed, Even though he asked a lot of us, he would let us have fun as well. “He was the loudest in the dressing rooms, so he gave you that kind of freedom. But, you had to back it up on the pitch working hard and doing what he asked. “He could create pictures. He made it really easy to understands where he wanted you to go and what he wanted you to do. It was like a movie in your head. “So, that kind of ability to get you motivated to do what you need to do, it’s what puts him above many others. He wanted us to play the most intense football. "It was hunt, hunt, hunt, always hunt. If you got the ball, run fast at your opponent as hard as possible. If they [the opponent] got the ball, go hunt it [back] again. "He would play games too, if we ran 120 kilometres [as a team] one week, next week he would say let’s do 124 [kilometres]. We believed in what he was saying. “Even though we lost games and derbies, he would say it doesn’t matter because he felt we were going in the right direction,” he said, speaking with a undeniable passion. Perhaps the proof is in the pudding. During his time at a once lowly BVB side, he transformed them into a deadly force which claimed two Bundesliga titles and a DFB-Pokal. Whether that can be replicated on the international stage is up for debate. However, in Owomoyela's mind, Klopp possesses the necessary traits to bring dreams into reality.

item.title: 'Absolutely embarrassing!' - Gary Neville slams Arsenal star Gabriel for 'play-acting' during Premier League victory over Liverpool
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Gary Neville has strongly criticised Arsenal defender Gabriel for his embarrassing play-acting during a vital Premier League victory over Liverpool at Anfield. The Brazilian went down clutching his face following a minor collision, prompting a fierce response from the former Manchester United captain on commentary. Gabriel criticised for Anfield theatrics Neville has accused Gabriel of embarrassing play-acting during Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool . Mikel Arteta's side secured a vital 1-0 win at Anfield to move three points clear at the top of the table. The controversy occurred in the opening minutes of the tense encounter following a physical collision between the Brazilian defender and Liverpool striker Alexander Isak. Gabriel immediately went down holding his face and appealed to referee Andy Madley for a foul. However, television replays quickly exposed the true nature of the incident involving the Arsenal centre-back. The footage clearly showed that Isak's arm had only made contact with Gabriel's upper chest rather than his face. Neville tears into the defender Neville was far from impressed with the theatrical reaction and voiced his frustration on Sky Sports commentary. The former United defender believes Gabriel must permanently remove this behaviour from his game. "He does let himself down at times," Neville stated. "I love his fire, his passion and his tenacity. But there’s a push into his upper chest and he goes down holding his face." Neville continued his assessment with a blunt final verdict on the Anfield incident. He added: "It’s absolutely embarrassing. He needs to stop doing that." Arsenal secure a massive away victory Despite the early controversy, Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game after 16 minutes to seal all three points. The narrow defeat was a bitter blow for Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, who remain fifth in the table and outside the Champions League places. Neville was quick to praise Arsenal for their resilience and tactical discipline following the final whistle. He highlighted the sheer magnitude of securing a clean sheet at such a notoriously difficult venue. "It was a defensive masterclass from Arsenal," Neville explained. "Andoni Iraola will be upset, he will feel like his team have given everything, but they put themselves right in the driving seat." European football returns for both clubs Arsenal must quickly shift their focus away from domestic matters as they prepare for a midweek European away trip. Arteta's men travel to the Czech Republic to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League, hoping to extend their excellent run of form. Liverpool also return to Champions League action in the coming days as they desperately look to bounce back from this frustrating league disappointment. Iraola will take his squad to Turkey for a highly challenging fixture against Fenerbahce.

item.title: 'It'll make us dizzy' - Gennaro Gattuso warns Lazio stars not to look at the Serie A table despite going top with comeback win over Cagliari
item.description: SS Lazio v Cagliari Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso has urged his players to ignore the Serie A standings despite moving clear at the summit with a 2-1 comeback win over Cagliari on Sunday. The Italian tactician insists his unbeaten side must remain grounded and prioritise reaching the 40-point mark after claiming a sixth consecutive league victory. Italian boss demands complete focus Gattuso refused to get carried away at the Stadio Olimpico even though the Biancocelesti sit top after 10 games for the first time since 2010-11. Sunday's triumph allowed the hosts to capitalise on Inter losing to AC Milan on Saturday . They have also recorded six straight league wins for the first time since Simone Inzaghi's reign in 2021. Late header seals comeback triumph Having netted 24 goals in their opening 10 fixtures for the first time since 2017-18, the hosts trailed to M'Bala Nzola's 20th-minute opener until Gustav Isaksen equalised in the 36th minute, setting the stage for substitute Andrea Pinamonti to head an 83rd-minute winner. Focusing on the club's 40-point target rather than the standings, Gattuso told DAZN Italia : "We are all up there, we still need 12 points to achieve the target of 40 that we set at the start of the season. "Every team in the league is balanced and well-structured, so we've got to keep taking it one game at a time and see where we end up. It is best that we don't look at the table right now, or it'll make us dizzy. We've got to push hard, rest, then push hard again." Unbeaten leaders show relentless spirit Alongside third-placed Roma, who sit four points behind under Gian Piero Gasperini, the leaders remain unbeaten in Serie A this season. Insisting his side must maintain their determination after responding to an earlier cup setback , Gattuso added: "That defeat didn't take away our belief in what we were doing, we don't let go. We work, we don't complain, this is the spirit that is pushing us on, because without that, we become a normal team." Crediting his substitutes for changing the contest against stubborn visitors, he continued: "It was a very difficult match and all credit for that goes to Cagliari, because we struggled and those who came off the bench changed the game with their mentality. This was a very important match for us, we did everything to take the result home. Cagliari are tough to deal with, they defend and attack well." Napoli test precedes international break Gattuso will now prepare his squad to face an out-of-form Napoli side in their final league match before the November international break. Maintaining their winning momentum will be vital as they seek to protect their cushion at the summit. Meanwhile, Cagliari must regroup quickly after suffering four straight top-flight defeats for the first time since April.

item.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Monday, November 2
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Archie Gray of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Crystal Palace FC at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) | Getty Images good morning everyone and welcome to november! The turning of the calendar means it’s time to Take a Look at the Month Ahead, where hoddle HQ checks out the month’s schedule for the men’s and women’s teams at Tottenham Hotspur Football Club. Tottenham Hotspur men’s squad: The boys enter November having won three games on the bounce. The last time they did that was more than 600 days ago. Is the tide beginning to turn? I never like those questions because I follow Tottenham Hotspur, and history cautions me against believing corners have been turned. But this month’s light selection of matches is temping. Oh boy, is it tempting. Still, I’m looking forward to a difficult match against Leeds United on 7th November. Leeds haven’t lost at home since March 3 (that was a 0-1 loss to Sunderland). This season, they’re 1-3-0 at home against mostly decent competition. Form like that is difficult to break down, so I’m quite cautious heading into this weekend. Then there are two matches against a surprisingly steady Ipswich Town and bottom-of-the-pack Sunderland. You might be surprise to learn Town have scored more goals than Spurs this season, although they have a -4 goal differential. Sunderland are looking pretty bad though, which isn’t surprising given the additional football they have to play in Europe. Seven points should be the minimum expectations, but I’ll accept nine points. November schedule: at Leeds (7 Nov); Ipswich Town (21 Nov); at Sunderland (29 Nov) Tottenham Hotspur women’s squad: A little bit of a different form for the ladies. A 4-1 win against Bournemouth on Sunday snapped an ugly three-game skid in league play in which they were outscored 14-4. That shows there’s still a large gap between Spurs and the rest of the league, even if they sit fourth. We’ve got a mixed bag this month. Brighton will be a good test, and I think there are some good opportunities for their League Cup group play before a big test against Manchester City to end the month. November schedule: Brighton (8 Nov); Crystal Place (11 Nov, Women’s League Cup); Everton (14 Nov); Leicester (18 Nov, Women’s League Cup); Man City (22 Nov) Fitzie’s track of the day: II B.S., by Charles Mingus And now for your links: Alasdair Gold : “The huge Luca Williams-Barnett mistake Tottenham can’t make and Van Hecke’s remarkable visitors” The Athletic ($$) : “Are Tottenham, at last, a good team again?” The Telegraph : “Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage” The Independent : “Police investigate fan taunt using Bradley Lowery photo during Coventry vs Sunderland”

item.title: Unai Emery: Manchester United have clear choice in tactical genius to replace Michael Carrick
item.description: Unai Emery: Manchester United have clear choice in tactical genius to replace Michael Carrick Manchester United fans had to face up to another loss on Saturday afternoon, this time coming against Chelsea. Current situation Michael Carrick’s job appears safe until the next international break, which begins in a week, but he must navigate matches against AS Roma and Aston Villa at Old Trafford. It is widely expected that Carrick will lose his job in the not-too-distant future, with the side sitting seventeenth in the league, above the drop zone on goal difference. There have been numerous names linked to the Old Trafford hot seat, such as Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Fabian Hürzeler. Nonetheless, one name that should also be one hundred percent on the club’s list is Unai Emery. Fabrizio Romano has stated that the club do in fact admire the Spaniard and he would be an incredible choice to replace Carrick. The case for Unai Emery Villa job The job Emery has done at Aston Villa is nothing short of spectacular. In the context of regularly having to sell his best players and failing to replace them with huge names, he continues to get his side firing. They won the Europa League last season and also finished fourth in the league. He has won 116 of his 211 matches at Aston Villa, boasting a win percentage of 55. The Spaniard is also a winner, as he has won five separate Europa Leagues: three with Sevilla, one with Villarreal and, of course, last season’s with Villa. Tactics What’s more, Emery is a strong tactician who regularly gets the best out of players. Villa lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins this summer, all crucial players to the first eleven. Most managers would crumble or throw their toys out of the pram. Emery’s response: second place in the Champions League with three wins from three. The league has been tougher going as they currently sit ninth, but showed their quality by beating Manchester City 2-1 two weekends ago. Emery has been described as a manager who is “the outstanding current example of the game-plan school: a stable structure underneath, an opponent-specific plan on top, and a depth of preparation that turns information into confidence.” He can be flexible and instructs his team to play with and without the ball with ease. The Spaniard is also famed for his tactical preparation, with “Emery’s weeks being built backwards from the opponent. Video analysis is the spine of preparation, hours of it, with the plan fed to players across the week through unit meetings, individual clips and walkthroughs rather than dumped on them the day before the game.” An itch to scratch at bigger clubs Finally, while it may be hard to see Emery walking away from the success he has built at Villa, he will have an itch to scratch at a truly massive football club. The case for Unai Emery Villa job The job Emery has done at Aston Villa is nothing short of spectacular. In the context of regularly having to sell his best players and failing to replace them with huge names, he continues to get his side firing. They won the Europa League last season and also finished fourth in the league. He has won 116 of his 211 matches at Aston Villa, boasting a win percentage of 55. The Spaniard is also a winner, as he has won five separate Europa Leagues: three with Sevilla, one with Villarreal and, of course, last season’s with Villa. Tactics What’s more, Emery is a strong tactician who regularly gets the best out of players. Villa lost Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins this summer, all crucial players to the first eleven. Most managers would crumble or throw their toys out of the pram. Emery’s response: second place in the Champions League with three wins from three. The league has been tougher going as they currently sit ninth, but showed their quality by beating Manchester City 2-1 two weekends ago. Emery has been described as a manager who is “the outstanding current example of the game-plan school: a stable structure underneath, an opponent-specific plan on top, and a depth of preparation that turns information into confidence.” He can be flexible and instructs his team to play with and without the ball with ease. The Spaniard is also famed for his tactical preparation, with “Emery’s weeks being built backwards from the opponent. Video analysis is the spine of preparation, hours of it, with the plan fed to players across the week through unit meetings, individual clips and walkthroughs rather than dumped on them the day before the game.” An itch to scratch at bigger clubs Finally, while it may be hard to see Emery walking away from the success he has built at Villa, he will have an itch to scratch at a truly massive football club. At Paris Saint-Germain, he did win one league, two national cups and two league cups. Nonetheless, as he did not win the Champions League, he was never given the respect he probably deserved in France. What’s more, his time at Arsenal is probably viewed as a failure given he lost the final of the Europa League and did not win a trophy. He could well see the United job as an attempt to finally gain recognition at one of the hottest seats in world football. Final thoughts There is no doubt extracting Emery from Villa could be difficult and expensive. What’s more, his style of football may not always bring United fans to their feet. Nonetheless, his tactical excellence, ability to build coherent teams according to the tools available to him, and his hunger to succeed at a truly giant global name make him an outstanding candidate to turn Manchester United’s sinking ship around. United fans will get another sample of his work this weekend when his Villa side travel to Old Trafford this coming Sunday. Featured image by Carl Recine via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns
item.description: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams ’ star cornerback Trent McDuffie briefly exited Sunday’s 24-9 win over the Los Angeles Chargers after sustaining a back injury. Head coach Sean McVay did not offer a clear diagnosis following the game; his initial reaction indicated that the team had reasons to remain optimistic about the defender’s condition. While speaking to reporters after the game, based on his initial observations, the Rams head coach offered an encouraging assessment of how the cornerback appeared to be feeling. “He looks like he’s feeling OK,” McVay said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McDuffie went down late in the third quarter after seemingly hurting his back while making a tackle in the backfield. He initially limped off the field and headed to the locker room for further evaluation before eventually making his way back to the sideline. Following the incident, the cornerback was initially listed as questionable to return. However, his appearance on the sideline later in the game offered some encouragement, as he seemed to be doing better after the injury scare. McDuffie had already missed Weeks 6 and 7 after suffering a groin injury during practice. Despite carrying a questionable designation heading into the matchup against the Chargers, he managed to return to action and contribute to the Rams’ defensive effort. Meanwhile, McDuffie was not the only Los Angeles cornerback to suffer an injury during Sunday’s game. Jaylen Watson also left the game in the third quarter with a shoulder issue and was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the matchup. Fortunately, the injury setbacks did not prevent the Rams from securing a comfortable victory and extending their winning streak to four games. Meanwhile, the Chargers remained winless after falling to 0-7 this season . The Rams will now have a full week to monitor McDuffie’s recovery before traveling to face the Washington Commanders in Week 9. Related: Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers Related: Rams’ Sean McVay laughs off Aaron Donald’s fumble recovery fail vs. Chargers

item.title: Vikings, Chiefs and Cowboys beaten - NFL week eight
item.description: Kyler Murray became Minnesota's starting quarterback after leaving Arizona while Gardner Minshew was signed to be the Cardinals' back-up [Getty Images] The Minnesota Vikings became the last NFL team to lose their unbeaten record as the 2026 season continued with a wild weekend. There were a number of rare occurrences during week eight while two games were settled in overtime. The Dallas Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs were both beaten after being stunned by late fightbacks while quarterback Joe Burrow was involved in six touchdowns as the Cincinnati Bengals won again. Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass. And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson. Here are the top stories from Sunday's action in the NFL. Jackson returns - but immediately injured again Lamar Jackson sustained his latest injury when his hand struck an opponent after throwing the ball [Getty Images] Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills. But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury. That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners. The Ravens have lost their past three games and now have a 4-4 record, and Jackson could miss the rest of the season as he is set to undergo surgery. This is the latest injury blow for Jackson. Although he is one of the most gifted players of his generation, the 29-year-old seems destined not to reach the Super Bowl during his career and the Ravens could miss out on the play-offs for a second straight year. Huntley could also be out for weeks so the Ravens will have to act fast to bring in an experienced QB or Fagnano will have to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. NFL's Campbell taken to hospital with neck injury Broncos replace Chiefs in top spot Minnesota put their 6-0 record on the line at their NFC North rivals the Detroit Lions, who won 19-15 to halt the Vikings' unbeaten start. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown as Detroit (5-2) prevailed in one of several key divisional match-ups. The Denver Broncos (6-2) replaced the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) at the top of the AFC West after coming from 11 points down in the final quarter to win 28-24. Patrick Mahomes threw for three touchdowns and 321 yards but that was not enough for the Chiefs as the Broncos' defence made a goal-line stand at the death to clinch victory. The Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) are in charge of the AFC South after romping to a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts, who look set for a rebuild. After

There were a number of rare occurrences during week eight while two games were settled in overtime. The Dallas Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs were both beaten after being stunned by late fightbacks while quarterback Joe Burrow was involved in six touchdowns as the Cincinnati Bengals won again. Otherwise running backs shone on Sunday, especially for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as they managed to claim victory without completing a single pass. And the Baltimore Ravens lost not one but two quarterbacks during their defeat by the Buffalo Bills, including the league's two-time Most Valuable Player, Lamar Jackson. Here are the top stories from Sunday's action in the NFL. Jackson returns - but immediately injured again Lamar Jackson sustained his latest injury when his hand struck an opponent after throwing the ball [Getty Images] Two former MVPs went head-to-head as Lamar Jackson returned from three games out with an ankle injury to face Josh Allen's Buffalo Bills. But that match-up was ruined within moments as Jackson injured his right thumb on the game's first snap, and his back-up Tyler Huntley was then ruled out in the second quarter with a toe injury. That meant they had to finish the game with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback and Buffalo ran out comfortable 36-10 winners. The Ravens have lost their past three games and now have a 4-4 record, and Jackson could miss the rest of the season as he is set to undergo surgery. This is the latest injury blow for Jackson. Although he is one of the most gifted players of his generation, the 29-year-old seems destined not to reach the Super Bowl during his career and the Ravens could miss out on the play-offs for a second straight year. Huntley could also be out for weeks so the Ravens will have to act fast to bring in an experienced QB or Fagnano will have to start against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. NFL's Campbell taken to hospital with neck injury Broncos replace Chiefs in top spot Minnesota put their 6-0 record on the line at their NFC North rivals the Detroit Lions, who won 19-15 to halt the Vikings' unbeaten start. Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and a touchdown as Detroit (5-2) prevailed in one of several key divisional match-ups. The Denver Broncos (6-2) replaced the Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) at the top of the AFC West after coming from 11 points down in the final quarter to win 28-24. Patrick Mahomes threw for three touchdowns and 321 yards but that was not enough for the Chiefs as the Broncos' defence made a goal-line stand at the death to clinch victory. The Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) are in charge of the AFC South after romping to a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts, who look set for a rebuild. After firing their general manager and trading two key players in the past two weeks, the Colts are reportedly in talks over trading star running back Jonathan Taylor. Meanwhile, the Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) beat the Cleveland Browns 26-7 to go top of the AFC North. Burrow firing for Bengals Another of Pittsburgh's divisional rivals, the Cincinnati Bengals, made hard work of it before beating the Tennessee Titans 43-36 in overtime. Despite being intercepted three times by Tennessee's Amani Hooker, Burrow became the first player in 75 years - and only the second ever after Norm van Brocklin's 554 passing yards in a 1951 game - to record more than 450 passing yards, five touchdown passes and a rushing touchdown in a single game. After a mixed start to the season, the former first overall draft pick has also become the first quarterback in NFL history to register a 70% completion percentage plus touchdown passes in three consecutive games. Burrow and his high-powered offence are in ominous form as they seek a Super Bowl return and host Pittsburgh in two weeks. Bucs win without making a pass The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran the ball 56 times while Atlanta had 28 carries for 99 yards [Getty Images] While Cincinnati's offence relies on its passing game and receivers, many of the NFL's running backs grabbed the spotlight on Sunday. For the first time since 2003, at least six players had 140 rushing yards on the same day, including Bucky Irving (170) and Kenneth Gainwell (140) as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0. Torrential rain in Florida made handling conditions difficult so Tampa Bay quarterback Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes, completing none of them. Instead he spent most of the day handing the ball to Irving or Gainwell as the Bucs racked up a team-record 324 rushing yards. They also became the first team to have zero pass completions since 1974 – and just the second in the Super Bowl era. 'Minshew Magic' stuns Cowboys Tyler Allgeier was the running back who starred for the Arizona Cardinals, rushing for 147 yards at the Dallas Cowboys. But it was eccentric back-up quarterback Gardner Minshew who helped turn the game in Arizona's favour after replacing an ineffective Jacoby Brissett with the Cardinals trailing 17-3 late in the third quarter. After being a late draft pick by Jacksonville in 2019, Minshew has spent most of his career as a back-up and in the off-season Arizona became his sixth team in eight years. He made a thrilling debut, though, becoming the first quarterback this season to throw three touchdown passes in a fourth quarter. That tied the game at the death, and although recent hero Chad Ryland failed to kick the extra point, he redeemed himself in overtime with a field goal to win 33-30. It is only the second time Dallas have ever lost when leading by 10 points inside the final three minutes and leaves them 3-5. It also heaps pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer, with outspoken team owner Jerry Jones saying: "It's an indictment of the whole show". item.title: Packers vs. Patriots odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
item.description: (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have opened up as 2.5-point road underdogs on FanDuel against the New England Patriots in Week 9, coming off a mini-bye after beating the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football . The Patriots had a little scare against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but were able to outscore Miami 21-6 in the second half to win 24-19. Overall, quarterback Drake Maye seems to have caught his groove after starting slowly to begin the 2026 season. Over the last four games, he’s posted MVP-type numbers, combining to throw 11 touchdowns to just one interception and crossing the 110 passer rating mark in each of those games. The Packers are also coming in relatively hot, mostly off the backs of their defense and offensive passing game, and have won four of their last five games after being embarrassed at home for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons. Both teams are fighting for something on Sunday, as the Patriots’ chances of winning the AFC East drop from 31 percent to just 21 percent if the Packers beat them, according to The Athletic’s playoff simulator . Green Bay’s path to the playoffs mostly involves a wild card spot at this point, as the team is being given just a seven percent chance of winning the division per the same simulator. According to The Athletic, the Packers have a 61 percent chance to make the playoffs if they beat the Patriots, but just a 39 percent chance if they lose. If Green Bay can split their trip to New England and their Week 10 game against the Minnesota Vikings, who are sitting in the driver’s seat in the NFC North at the moment, they have about a 50-50 chance of making the playoffs going into their Week 11 bye week. After that, they should be getting some players back from injury lists, notably edge rusher Micah Parsons. Go Pack Go—wherever you go! item.title: Cardinals’ Gardner Minsew highlights team’s perfect response to Chad Ryland’s FG miss
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Cardinals’ Gardner Minsew highlights team’s perfect response to Chad Ryland’s FG miss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals found themselves in the middle of pure gridiron chaos during Week 8 against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. Backup quarterback Gardner Minshew came off the bench in the third quarter for Jacoby Brissett and engineered a thrilling late comeback, connecting with wide receiver Michael Wilson on a 13-yard touchdown pass with just 6 seconds remaining in regulation. However, what should have been a regulation victory turned into overtime drama when kicker Chad Ryland pulled the potential game-winning extra point wide left. Instead of letting the missed kick deflate the sideline, Minshew immediately rallied the locker room with his trademark infectious energy. Speaking with reporters after the game, Minshew broke down how the team quickly wiped the slate clean. “Two or thirty thirty got a chance to go play these boys in overtime, let’s freaking go. You know, sign me up,” Minshew said. “So I think that’s how quick can you reset, how quick can you, cause I think that this is a game that was a total testament to that you know. Forget what happened before, forget everything that’s happened to this point. Just keep going, keep giving yourselves a chance and we had a group of fighters today that was a lot of fun to go with.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Gardner Minshew when asked how he keeps leading the team following Ryland’s missed XP near the end of regulation A very Minshew answer. Great stuff #AZCardinals pic.twitter.com/wfPM5VmN98 — Dom Tibbetts (@DomTibbettsTV) November 1, 2026 Minshew’s unbreakable mindset paid off instantly in the extra frame. After replacing Brissett, the veteran signal-caller put together a masterful performance, completing 17 of 23 passes for 188 yards and 3 touchdowns. Running back Tyler Allgeier added explosive power to the offense, rushing for 147 yards on 11 carries to help Arizona outgain Dallas 467-261. After the Cardinals’ defense forced a punt in overtime, Minshew marched the offense 44 yards downfield. That set up Ryland for a 42-yard field goal attempt, and the kicker split the uprights to redeem himself and lock up a 33-30 victory. Minshew’s poise under pressure proved that no matter how bizarre the circumstances get, Arizona always has a puncher’s chance. Related: Cardinals Mike LaFleur gets real about decision to switch to Gardner Minshew vs. Cowboys Related: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur won’t commit to Gardner Minshew as Week 9 starter despite Cowboys heroics

item.title: Steelers’ Jaquan Brisker hits Deshaun Watson with ‘babying’ jab after beating Browns
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Steelers’ Jaquan Brisker hits Deshaun Watson with ‘babying’ jab after beating Browns appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers dominated the Cleveland Browns on Sunday , but Jaquan Brisker was not done going after Deshaun Watson even after the final whistle. On the third play of the game, the Steelers safety hit Watson high and was flagged for roughing the passer, handing Cleveland a fresh set of downs. The hit sent Watson to the medical tent for a concussion evaluation , and Shedeur Sanders stepped in for the rest of the series. Watson passed the evaluation and returned for the Browns’ next drive, but Brisker clearly did not think much of the call. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Babying the quarterback. He’s over there crying or whatever he’s doing. It is what it is,” Brisker said, via Ashley Wensk of KDKA-TV . Jaquan Brisker on getting flagged for roughing the passer for his hit on Deshaun Watson on the opening drive of Steelers/Browns "Babying the quarterback. He's over there crying or whatever he's doing. It is what it is." "He had his binky today, so." pic.twitter.com/6epqtF60Zd — Ashley Wenskoski (@AshleyWenskTV) November 1, 2026 Brisker then added another jab: “He had his binky today, so.” The flag aside, it was a long day for Watson and the Browns at Acrisure Stadium. Pittsburgh cruised to a 27-6 win, sacking Watson eight times and holding Cleveland out of the end zone for the first time this season. Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without a touchdown or an interception, but the Browns could not get anything going on the ground, finishing with just 34 rushing yards on 15 carries. Cleveland also lost two fumbles, while Pittsburgh’s defense racked up 13 quarterback hits and forced four three-and-outs. The Steelers, meanwhile, piled up 200 rushing yards. Rico Dowdle opened the scoring with a 9-yard touchdown run, Pat Freiermuth punched in a 1-yard score just before halftime and Jaylen Warren added another 1-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to make it 27-6. The win was a measure of revenge for Pittsburgh, which fell 27-24 to the Browns on Thursday Night Football in Week 4 . The Steelers improved to 6-2 and have now won four straight games, while the Browns dropped to 5-3. Brisker has quickly made his presence felt in Pittsburgh. The former second-round pick spent his first four seasons with the Chicago Bears before signing a one-year, $5.5 million deal with the Steelers in March . His comments will likely add even more fuel to an already heated AFC North rivalry. The Steelers will have a week off before visiting the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football on Nov. 15. Related: Steelers’ Jaylen Warren throws shade at Jared Verse after dog-walking Browns Related: Steelers’ Cam Heyward scoffs at Jared Verse drama after smacking Browns

item.title: Mike McCarthy reveals Steelers’ Tush Push nickname, and it’s an ode to Penn State
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Mike McCarthy reveals Steelers’ Tush Push nickname, and it’s an ode to Penn State appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers have a name for their version of the tush push . They call it the “Nittany Package,” a nod to tight end Pat Freiermuth’s Penn State background. Pittsburgh beat Cleveland 27-6 on Sunday. With five seconds left, the Steelers had the ball at the 1-yard line. Aaron Rodgers chose to go for a touchdown instead of a field goal. Freiermuth took the direct snap and followed center Zach Frazier into the end zone. Tight end Darnell Washington and running back Jaylen Warren pushed him from behind. It gave Pittsburgh a 20-6 lead and was Freiermuth’s first rushing touchdown in six NFL seasons. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCarthy said Rodgers made the call . “Aaron called that play,” McCarthy said. “Obviously, everybody agreed with it. But the whole mechanics leading up to that, I think that just shows the confidence they have and, obviously, Aaron’s experience of handling those situations.” The Steelers have used the Nittany Package four times and converted on every attempt. They previously ran it on fourth-and-1 against the Patriots and Colts, and on third-and-1 against the Bengals. Sunday was their first attempt from the goal line. According to Rodgers, he was not leaving the field without trying to score. Pittsburgh had no timeouts left, so a failed attempt would have ended the half. Troy Fautanu also called it his favorite play. Pittsburgh had earlier failed to score from the Browns’ 2-yard line and settled for a field goal. McCarthy said he wished he could have those three plays back. But the Nittany Package worked when the Steelers tried it again on Sunday. item.content:encoded: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Mike McCarthy reveals Steelers’ Tush Push nickname, and it’s an ode to Penn State appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers have a name for their version of the tush push . They call it the “Nittany Package,” a nod to tight end Pat Freiermuth’s Penn State background. Pittsburgh beat Cleveland 27-6 on Sunday. With five seconds left, the Steelers had the ball at the 1-yard line. Aaron Rodgers chose to go for a touchdown instead of a field goal. Freiermuth took the direct snap and followed center Zach Frazier into the end zone. Tight end Darnell Washington and running back Jaylen Warren pushed him from behind. It gave Pittsburgh a 20-6 lead and was Freiermuth’s first rushing touchdown in six NFL seasons. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McCarthy said Rodgers made the call . “Aaron called that play,” McCarthy said. “Obviously, everybody agreed with it. But the whole mechanics leading up to that, I think that just shows the confidence they have and, obviously, Aaron’s experience of handling those situations.” The Steelers have used the Nittany Package four times and converted on every attempt. They previously ran it on fourth-and-1 against the Patriots and Colts, and on third-and-1 against the Bengals. Sunday was their first attempt from the goal line. According to Rodgers, he was not leaving the field without trying to score. Pittsburgh had no timeouts left, so a failed attempt would have ended the half. Troy Fautanu also called it his favorite play. Pittsburgh had earlier failed to score from the Browns’ 2-yard line and settled for a field goal. McCarthy said he wished he could have those three plays back. But the Nittany Package worked when the Steelers tried it again on Sunday. item.title: Raiders’ Kirk Cousins breaks silence on ‘wellness celly’ after TD vs. Jets
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) gets ready under center as the New York Jets play Las Vegas Raiders in a week 8 NFL football game at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in East Rutherford, NJ. Raiders’ Kirk Cousins breaks silence on ‘wellness celly’ after TD vs. Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Kirk Cousins led the Las Vegas Raiders to a 38-33 road win over the New York Jets that came after a 23-14 halftime deficit that was sparked by a big day through the air from Brock Bowers . Coach Klint Kubiak commented on Ashton Jeanty ’s surprisingly low workload while Kirk Cousins was in a happy mood as he discussed his recently unveiled “wellness celly.” The Cousins celebration was on display with the Raiders trailing 30-21. Cousins mimicked an elbow massage as the Raiders attempted to claw their way back into the game. He talked to Megan Olivi about the move as fans watched. “We played through (adversity)…This league’s gonna test ya…I call that my wellness celebration, I told (teammates) if I had a rushing touchdown I’d do it, and Brock Bowers as I was jogging off the field, I wouldn’t have thought to do it, he goes, ‘Hit ’em with a wellness celly!’ So I did it.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cousins had over 200 yards and three touchdown passes as he focused on throwing to Bowers, Jeanty and Michael Mayer, working the field in sublime fashion as he led the Raiders back with possible replacement and 2026 NFL Draft first round pick Fernando Mendoza looking on. Jeanty took serious heat from Rex Ryan before the game about his comments on the Jets’ tackling abilities. He gave way to Mike Washington Jr. in the run game and he responded with 25 carries for 83 yards. Bowers had 92 yards and two touchdowns as the Raiders moved to 4-4. November 8 brings a home game against the San Francisco 49ers that will give Cousins a chance to take the starting QB job by the horns and restore confidence in fans moving forward. Related: Raiders news: Only 1 thing surprises Klint Kubiak about Brock Bowers after another big day Related: What Raiders’ Klint Kubiak said about turning to Mike Washington Jr. with Ashton Jeanty in doghouse

item.title: Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams kept the Los Angeles Chargers winless, running away with a convincing win, 24-9, at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. The Rams improved to 4-4 , while the Chargers fell to 0-7. The Rams bucked a slow start, with Matthew Stafford throwing 17-of-25 for 157 yards and one touchdown, and Puka Nacua getting 11 receptions for 80 yards and a touchdown. After the encouraging performance, Nacua stressed that the Rams can still turn it up a notch, especially on offense, and go on a hot streak, according to the Los Angeles Daily News’ Adam Grosbard. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “This is something that we gotta be able to continue to build upon, but it’s not something that we can exhale from. There’s still a lot of improvement. If our defense is playing their butts off like that, we gotta be able to go out there and play complementary football,” said the 25-year-old wide receiver. The Rams lead the league with 411 yards per game. They average 24.3 points per outing, which is 10th in the NFL. The offense looked lethargic at the outset against the Chargers , failing to get a first down on their first five drives for the first time under coach Sean McVay. They went into the halftime break with a one-point lead, 10-9. The defense held down the fort, shutting down the Chargers in the second half. Justin Herbert finished 24-of-32 for zero touchdowns and two interceptions. He was sacked twice. The Rams won back-to-back games for the first time since January, beating the Las Vegas Raiders, 35-21, in Week 7. They will try to maintain their winning streak when they visit the Washington Commanders in Week 9. Related: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns Related: Rams’ Sean McVay laughs off Aaron Donald’s fumble recovery fail vs. Chargers

item.title: George Furbank: ‘A few people have said I need to go and see a witch doctor’
item.description: “A few people have said that I need to go and see a witch doctor,” George Furbank chuckles, perhaps to hide a grimace beneath after two years of misfortune. Rugby has known a few tales of black cats and broken mirrors but not many players have endured such a wretched run that has meant an absence from 20 consecutive England Tests in the prime of the full-back’s career. First came a broken arm in December of 2024; then a concussion; then a niggly calf injury he struggled to shake. In July, Furbank was named in the No 15 shirt for England’s encounter with South Africa only to be rushed to hospital to have his appendix removed – matchday was spent not at Ellis Park but in a rather different kind of Johannesburg theatre. “Do I believe in luck?” Furbank ponders, repeating the question I have posed with a contemplative pause. One would forgive an answer of frustration at this apparent cosmic misalignment but the 30-year-old is not that way minded. “Not really,” he continues. “It’s pretty cliche but I think you make your own luck. George Furbank has endured a tough two years (Getty) “Could you say I’ve been unlucky with the injuries and the timing? Potentially, but most boys will go through periods of injuries. Unfortunately, mine have been a bit back-to-back. The last two years have definitely been tough. I haven’t been able to play, or in good enough form to play, as much as I’d like to. But it has made me realise how much I do love coming here. I’m so desperate to be back on the international stage and pull on an England shirt again. When it gets taken away from you, you realise how much you miss it.” How England have missed Furbank, too. Their form may have fluctuated in the nearly two years since he won the last of his 14 caps against Japan but there has been a sense throughout that they might be a better side with the full-back in it. It is a mark of Steve Borthwick ’s faith in the player that he has remained a contracted player throughout his injury trials and tribulations; all will hope for a clean bill of health throughout this November. Furbank has suffered a number of different injuries (PA Wire) It has been a year of change in other ways for Furbank. If it was a wrench to leave Northampton with club and captain unable to reach agreement on mutually beneficial terms, another Gallagher Prem title was a perfect farewell , and Furbank has settled well at Harlequins. A house in Wimbledon has fulfilled a life-long dream to live in London – if Northampton had its small-town charm, the comparative cornucopia on his new doorstep is providing a welcome alternative. “Finishing the way I did at Saints was special, and a pretty cool way to close that chapter in my life. item.content:encoded: “A few people have said that I need to go and see a witch doctor,” George Furbank chuckles, perhaps to hide a grimace beneath after two years of misfortune. Rugby has known a few tales of black cats and broken mirrors but not many players have endured such a wretched run that has meant an absence from 20 consecutive England Tests in the prime of the full-back’s career. First came a broken arm in December of 2024; then a concussion; then a niggly calf injury he struggled to shake. In July, Furbank was named in the No 15 shirt for England’s encounter with South Africa only to be rushed to hospital to have his appendix removed – matchday was spent not at Ellis Park but in a rather different kind of Johannesburg theatre. “Do I believe in luck?” Furbank ponders, repeating the question I have posed with a contemplative pause. One would forgive an answer of frustration at this apparent cosmic misalignment but the 30-year-old is not that way minded. “Not really,” he continues. “It’s pretty cliche but I think you make your own luck. George Furbank has endured a tough two years (Getty) “Could you say I’ve been unlucky with the injuries and the timing? Potentially, but most boys will go through periods of injuries. Unfortunately, mine have been a bit back-to-back. The last two years have definitely been tough. I haven’t been able to play, or in good enough form to play, as much as I’d like to. But it has made me realise how much I do love coming here. I’m so desperate to be back on the international stage and pull on an England shirt again. When it gets taken away from you, you realise how much you miss it.” How England have missed Furbank, too. Their form may have fluctuated in the nearly two years since he won the last of his 14 caps against Japan but there has been a sense throughout that they might be a better side with the full-back in it. It is a mark of Steve Borthwick ’s faith in the player that he has remained a contracted player throughout his injury trials and tribulations; all will hope for a clean bill of health throughout this November. Furbank has suffered a number of different injuries (PA Wire) It has been a year of change in other ways for Furbank. If it was a wrench to leave Northampton with club and captain unable to reach agreement on mutually beneficial terms, another Gallagher Prem title was a perfect farewell , and Furbank has settled well at Harlequins. A house in Wimbledon has fulfilled a life-long dream to live in London – if Northampton had its small-town charm, the comparative cornucopia on his new doorstep is providing a welcome alternative. “Finishing the way I did at Saints was special, and a pretty cool way to close that chapter in my life. But this has rejuvenated me,” Furbank explains. “A new challenge, new coaches, new players, a bit of a different way of playing. That group at Saints was so tight. We did stuff with each other every single day off. “I was a little bit worried – the boys are spread across so many different areas of London. Is it going to be that same feeling? It is a little bit different because boys are everywhere. But there’s still a really good environment. There’s always someone wanting to go for coffee.” The Hand-in-Hand pub on the common and Demitasse on the high street are becoming regular haunts. Furbank signed off with a second Prem title at Northampton (Getty) Alas, certain things did travel south with Furbank. His first outing in the quarters was over almost before it began after being knocked out by a stray knee against Edinburgh – “A good start to my Quins career! 30 seconds into my first game…” – and a delayed debut in the Prem for his new employers ended with a 48-0 thrashing by Gloucester. But things are starting to turn: Furbank was an influential presence in wins over Saracens and Exeter , and Harlequins have made a strong start in the Challenge Cup, a competition of real focus this season. The 30-year-old sees a resemblance to the struggles Saints experienced before the transformative impact of Chris Boyd, Phil Dowson and Sam Vesty, and hopes for a similarly effective turnaround. He is enjoying, too, the chance to combine more closely with Marcus Smith, a kindred spirit. “He’s world class to work with. He does things on the pitch that not many people can do. His dedication off the pitch in constantly improving his game is special as well.” Furbank has settled well at Harlequins (Getty) Could their alliance be reprised internationally? Regardless of the exact personnel, England’s playmaking partnership will surely be key to their Nations Championship fortunes. Borthwick’s squad are under no illusions that these Tests will be tighter and tougher than the games experienced in a fast and loose start to the Prem campaign, but a capacity to create and exploit space will clearly be vital. Furbank, though, wants no part of the criticism that has accompanied a high-scoring first phase of the season. “It kind of does my head in a bit. You have a season where there is a lot of kicking and defences are dominant, everyone moans about that. Then you have a 71-48 game, people are moaning about that. Find something to enjoy! “I watched that Saints-Bath game and could appreciate some unbelievable attack on show. But then you watch Gloucester-Bath, which is again incredible to watch but completely different. Why can’t you appreciate both? Teams are going to play differently depending on how they think they can get the best out of their players. Furbank last featured for England in November 2024 (Getty) “You watch the NRL and it always seems focused on, ‘how good was that?’ I think if you look at everything negatively the whole time, you don’t get any enjoyment or excitement out of the game. Yes, there are bits you have got to critique, don’t get me wrong, but I also think we can be way more positive in how we play and watch the game.” It is with that positive mindset that Furbank intends to attack the year ahead. Having made his debut in the Six Nations after the 2019 World Cup but fallen out of favour by the time of the next tournament, a trip to Australia next year is in the back of his mind. He can just about recall England’s last World Cup Down Under – the 2002/03 triumph. Furbank hopes to be part of England's squad at next year's World Cup (Getty) “I’d have been seven. I remember bits. I was down at Huntingdon Rugby Club watching it in a full clubhouse. I remember being quite overwhelmed when that drop goal went over; I think beer went flying everywhere, which probably wasn’t what a seven-year-old needed… “I don’t actively think about it but it is something in the background that is on my mind. It’s one of the goals I’ve got left in rugby: to go to a World Cup with England, and win a World Cup with England. That is the pinnacle of anyone’s career. It’s something that would be an absolute dream. To be that team to go and win it again would be incredibly special.”

item.title: 10 Eagles things I think I think from the loss to the Commanders
item.description: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts to a unnecessary roughness penalty by K'lavon Chaisson #45 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles certainly put up a performance for the ages on Sunday Night Football. This was a game where the Eagles needed a win to salvage a season that was on the verge of cratering, and they certainly imploded. Philadelphia’s offense barely mustered 10 points against the Washington Commanders in a 27-10 loss, while the defense allowed 27 unanswered points after the Eagles took a 10-0 lead late in the first quarter. The Eagles weren’t even competitive against a Commanders team that had just 1 win heading into November. That’s how bad this Eagles team is. While the season isn’t at the halfway point yet, this Eagles season is essentially over. There’s little confidence this team is going to make a run in the lowly NFC East, not with how poor they have played during this six-game losing streak (which is the longest by this franchise since 2012). The Eagles have started 2-6 for the first time since 1999, and there are a lot of aspects from this horrendous performance that need to be dissected. Buckle up. There are some hard truths coming regarding this football team. 1) This offensive line has gotten significantly worse under Chris Kuper. Jeff Stoutland might be the best assistant coach in franchise history. The Eagles were never going to replace him. Unfortunately, the Eagles found an offensive line coach that doesn’t improve his players — at all. Under Kuper, two of the five starting offensive linemen (Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen) from last season have gotten worse and the two young players (Markel Bell and Drew Kendall) are struggling to improve week in and week out. Bell was abysmal against the Commanders, allowing a 7.0% pressure rate and two sacks while getting dominated by K’Lavon Chaisson all night. Replacing Lane Johnson in a rookie season is a tough task, but Bell is not ready to be a starting right tackle in the NFL. That’s on Kuper and how he’s developing a rookie who is learning how to play right tackle for the first time in his football life. Dickerson allowed a sack and a 4.7% pressure rate, and his pressure rate is 7.8% in the three games he played this seaosn. This was a Pro Bowl player under Stoutland and now he’s a replacement level guard. Jordan Mailata’s performance is even diminishing, as he allowed a 7.0% pressure rate against the Commanders in what wa shis worst game of the season. If the Eagles do decide to move on from a coach this month, Kuper should be the first candidate. 2) The Eagles were right about Tanner McKee this summer. McKee lost out to Andy Dalton in the battle for the QB2 job for a reason. There is enough tape in the three games to demonstrate McKee isn’t good enough to be a starting quarterback
item.content:encoded: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts to a unnecessary roughness penalty by K'lavon Chaisson #45 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles certainly put up a performance for the ages on Sunday Night Football. This was a game where the Eagles needed a win to salvage a season that was on the verge of cratering, and they certainly imploded. Philadelphia’s offense barely mustered 10 points against the Washington Commanders in a 27-10 loss, while the defense allowed 27 unanswered points after the Eagles took a 10-0 lead late in the first quarter. The Eagles weren’t even competitive against a Commanders team that had just 1 win heading into November. That’s how bad this Eagles team is. While the season isn’t at the halfway point yet, this Eagles season is essentially over. There’s little confidence this team is going to make a run in the lowly NFC East, not with how poor they have played during this six-game losing streak (which is the longest by this franchise since 2012). The Eagles have started 2-6 for the first time since 1999, and there are a lot of aspects from this horrendous performance that need to be dissected. Buckle up. There are some hard truths coming regarding this football team. 1) This offensive line has gotten significantly worse under Chris Kuper. Jeff Stoutland might be the best assistant coach in franchise history. The Eagles were never going to replace him. Unfortunately, the Eagles found an offensive line coach that doesn’t improve his players — at all. Under Kuper, two of the five starting offensive linemen (Landon Dickerson and Tyler Steen) from last season have gotten worse and the two young players (Markel Bell and Drew Kendall) are struggling to improve week in and week out. Bell was abysmal against the Commanders, allowing a 7.0% pressure rate and two sacks while getting dominated by K’Lavon Chaisson all night. Replacing Lane Johnson in a rookie season is a tough task, but Bell is not ready to be a starting right tackle in the NFL. That’s on Kuper and how he’s developing a rookie who is learning how to play right tackle for the first time in his football life. Dickerson allowed a sack and a 4.7% pressure rate, and his pressure rate is 7.8% in the three games he played this seaosn. This was a Pro Bowl player under Stoutland and now he’s a replacement level guard. Jordan Mailata’s performance is even diminishing, as he allowed a 7.0% pressure rate against the Commanders in what wa shis worst game of the season. If the Eagles do decide to move on from a coach this month, Kuper should be the first candidate. 2) The Eagles were right about Tanner McKee this summer. McKee lost out to Andy Dalton in the battle for the QB2 job for a reason. There is enough tape in the three games to demonstrate McKee isn’t good enough to be a starting quarterback in the league. Even with the offensive line decimated by injuries and a poor offensive line, McKee is slow in his progressions and has no mobility to get out of trouble. McKee was abysmal against the Commanders, finishing 23-of-34 for 212 yards with 0 TD, 1 INT and a 72.2 passer rating. He also had a lost fumble in the second half, giving McKee two giveaways on the night. The numbers should have been worse, but 46 passing yards where in garbage time in the final minute to Eli Stowers. Since McKee made his first start in Week 6, he’s completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with 2 TD, 2 INT, and a 76.6 passer rating. McKee is 31st out of 32 quarterbacks in yards per attempt (5.6) and 26th in passer rating. The Eagles offense are 32nd in yards per play (4.2) in the three games with McKee as the starting quarterback, 31st in yards per attempt (5.6), and 29th in offensive points per game (15.0). McKee isn’t the answer as a starting quarterback. He may not even be a QB2 at this rate. The Eagles could try Joe Milton, but the offense won’t move the ball with him either. 3) The second half offense still stinks. Another week the Eagles offense struggled in the second half. Before the Eagles hit the garbage time portion of the game (27-10), the offense ran 32 plays for 91 yards with two giveaways, a missed field goal, and zero points — an abysmal 2.8 yards per play. Whether Jalen Hurts or Tanner McKee is the quarterback, this offense doesn’t move the ball. The Eagles average just 4.6 points per game in the second half, which is last in the nFL. The Eagles are also last in yards per play (3.9), yards per game (116.3), and yards per attempt (5.5). They are 29th in yards per carry (3.4), 30th in passer rating (70.4), and 29th in sack rate allowed (10.4%). McKee was 10-of-14 for 58 yards with 0 TD, 1 INT and a 49.1 passer rating in the second half prior to the garbage time possession at the end of the game — 4.1 yards per attempt. He led the Eagles with 16 rushing yards in the second half at that point, as Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell had 11 carries for 29 yards. Simply put, the Eagles aren’t making adjustments. 4) The second half defense is slightly better. This unit is bad too. They just aren’t at the very bottom of the league like the offense is. The Eagles are 30th in the NFL in points per game allowed (14.1) and 31st in yards per game allowed (198.1). They are 29th in yards per play allowed (5.9) and 32nd in rush yards per game allowed (78.1). The pass rush in the second half isn’t good either, as they are 27th in pressure rate (29.9%) and 27th in sack rate (4.6%). The pass defense is 29th in yards per attempt allowed (8.0). Again, they aren’t at the very bottom of the league. The second half defense is just near the bottom. This is a huge reason why the 2026 Eagles lose football games. 5) In conclusion… The Eagles are arguably the worst second half team in all of football, being outscored 113 to 37 in the second half of games this season. That -76 point differential isn’t even the worst in the NFL, as the Baltimore Ravens sit at -87 following their blowout loss to the Buffalo Bills this week (and the Ravens are on their third-string quarterback too). The yardage differential in the second half of games is -655, worst in the league. The next closest team are the Ravens at -629. The time of possession margin is -2.55 (29th), while the points per drive is 0.84 (32nd), and the three-and-out percentage is 50.0% (32nd). The explosive plays aren’t even there, as the 2.9% 20+ yard play percentage is 32nd in the league. Somehow the Eagles get worse in the second half of games. The personnel isn’t there (at least on one side of the ball), but the struggles go much deeper than that. 6) The run defense is making history. Another week the Eagles defense has allowed 100+ rushing yards to an opponent, as the Commanders had 135 rushing yards against a run defense that was supposed to be a strength of this team entering the year. Instead, the run defense is historically bad — and on the wrong side of history. The Eagles have allowed 100+ rushing yards in each of the first eight games of a season for the first time since 1968, and only the second time in the Super Bowl era. That 1968 team was one of the worst in franchise history, as the Eagles started 0-11 and finished 2-12. They weren’t even bad enough to get the No. 1 pick that year, and the fanbase booed Santa Claus that December as a result. The Eagles have allowed 1,055 rushing yards through eight games, third most in the NFL. The 131.9 rushing yards per game is also 30th, and the most by an Eagles team through eight games since 1998 (146.3). That 1998 Eagles team finished 3-13. This Eagles team is staring at a record that bad based on how poor the run defense is. 7) It’s time to protect Saquon Barkley from himself. Barkley deserves plenty of credit for fighting through his hamstring and back injuries and gutting out performances f

The issue remains finding a fifth striker, a topic back in the spotlight following the attacking crisis caused by injuries to Lautaro Martinez , Bonny and Pio Esposito. Inter had already assessed several options in the summer but chose not to proceed because they were unconvinced by the players available. The goalkeeper will not return until after the international break, while the number seven is expected to be sidelined until January. Dybala and Koné, meanwhile, hope to recover for Saturday's match against Sassuolo. Gollini will remain in goal, while Mancini is ready to return in defence alongside Ndicka and Hermoso. De Roon and Cristante will continue their midfield partnership, with Malen and Soulé guaranteed places in attack. The main doubts concern the flanks, where Wesley is certain to start, but which side he plays on remains to be decided: Lulli, Rensch and Molina are in contention. The Biancocelesti initially fell behind at the Olimpico but turned the game around thanks to goals from Isaksen and Pinamonti , maintaining the fine form of Gattuso 's side. The evening also marked the return of Danilo Cataldi , who finally made his first appearance of the season. The midfielder settled into the game well but was seen limping at the final whistle. According to Lazio Style Channel , the number 32 suffered heavy bruising: it does not appear to be a cause for concern, but further checks will be needed in the coming hours to assess his condition. 😕 Fiorentina: Fagioli and Oulai together? Nicolò Fagioli remains a mainstay for Fiorentina, with 734 minutes played and 10 starts in the first 11 matches of the season. Among outfield players, only Mastantuono, Ndour and Dragusin have played more minutes. However, criticism following the Atalanta match, combined with Oulai 's impressive performance off the bench, has reignited the debate over whether they can play together. In the first two and a half months, the pair shared the pitch for just 80 minutes across three defeats: Genoa was the only game they started together. As reported by Corriere dello Sport , Vanoli is looking for a way to accommodate both, but the team's midfield struggles have so far limited his experiments. One possibility is to give Oulai the deep-lying playmaker role, moving Fagioli into a wider central midfield position, with Ndour or Brescianini on the other side. Trials could be postponed until after the international break, while the club are already considering further midfield reinforcements ahead of the January transfer window. item.title: Hansi Flick set to repeat Barcelona defensive experiment against Aston Villa – report
item.description: Hansi Flick set to repeat Barcelona defensive experiment against Aston Villa – report Barcelona manager Hansi Flick could once again turn to Frenkie de Jong and Brian Farinas in unfamiliar defensive roles when the Catalans host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday, November 3. According to a report from AS , the German coach is considering retaining the makeshift defensive combination after it helped Barcelona secure a 6-1 victory over Alaves at Camp Nou . Flick’s decision against Alaves was dictated by an injury crisis that has left Barcelona short of defensive options. On that note, the likes of Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen were unavailable, while Xavi Espart was also among the absentees. With limited alternatives, the manager deployed De Jong at left centre-back and handed Farinas his first-team debut at right-back, despite the youngster being a midfielder by trade. Barcelona defensive injuries leave Flick with limited options The situation has forced Flick to experiment with the available options as he attempts to maintain defensive stability during an important period of the season. Frenkie de Jong played as a centre-back against Alaves. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) De Jong’s technical quality makes him a useful option when Barcelona need to build attacks from the back, although playing regularly as a centre-back would be a significant change to his responsibilities. Farinas, meanwhile, has an opportunity to demonstrate his versatility after being trusted with an unexpected first-team assignment. Barcelona’s 6-1 victory over Alaves offered encouragement, but the result does not necessarily mean the experimental defensive partnership has resolved the team’s underlying problems. In fact, the expectation is that the challenge against Aston Villa will provide a different level of examination. Farinas faces competition despite impressive debut Farinas’ involvement is particularly interesting because competition for midfield places at Barcelona is already intense. On that note, De Jong, Pedri, Gavi, Marc Bernal and Rodri are among the options ahead of him, while Espart can also operate in midfield. Brian Farinas made his Barcelona debut as a right-back. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Consequently, the youngster’s route into the senior side could be strengthened through his ability to cover multiple positions. Flick appears to value that flexibility, and the Alaves appearance provided an opportunity to assess him at a higher level. item.title: Stats: Real Madrid playmaker dominates La Liga creative charts as influence grows under Mourinho
item.description: Stats: Real Madrid playmaker dominates La Liga creative charts as influence grows under Mourinho Real Madrid have seen a massive turnaround in their fortunes in the last few weeks, making it six wins in a row with victory over Racing Santander. Los Blancos came flying out of the blocks at El Sardinero and scored three goals in the first half, which was enough for them to secure the three points. Among the many players who had a great game was Arda Guler, who continued his impressive start to the season. While Kylian Mbappe continues to dominate the goalscoring headlines, the Turkish international is quietly establishing himself as the creative spark of the team. Guler leads La Liga in two creative statistics Guler has registered 39 key passes and 21 accurate crosses this season, leading La Liga in both metrics. His numbers underline just how important and undroppable he has become for Jose Mourinho, making that right-wing position his own. The 21-year-old has also accumulated 4.32 expected assists (xA), the second-highest tally in the competition. His tally of 12 big chances created also places him second among La Liga players this season. Despite these numbers, the Turkish international has only three assists to his name, including one in the 3-0 victory over Racing. Against Racing, Guler provided a perfectly weighted through ball for Jude Bellingham’s well-taken goal. Three assists don’t paint the whole picture Guler’s underlying numbers suggest his influence and assist tally should have been much greater than just three. Expected assists is a measure of the quality of chances he has created, and the fact that his actual assists fall short of that figure suggests his teammates have not been clinical enough. Most leading assist providers in football tend to register more assists than their xA suggests, but Guler is an exception. Arda Guler has been Real Madrid’s creative force this season. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) However, if the finishing falls into place, it is encouraging that Guler’s underlying numbers are so promising. Mourinho trusts him a lot, and his ability to drift inside, identify passing lanes and deliver inch-perfect crosses provides the perfect balance for Madrid’s transitional attackers. Guler is also an exceptional set-piece taker, always posing a threat from both free kicks and corners. The 21-year-old is slowly evolving from a talented youngster into one of the first names on Mourinho’s team sheet , and it remains to be seen how he fares over the course of the season.

item.title: No Grealish, no cry - the rise of Everton's youngsters
item.description: Players aged 24 or under are playing a higher proportion of minutes for Everton this season [Getty Images] As Everton prepared to face Newcastle in the fourth round of the EFL Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, the stakes were high. A quarter-final tie against League Two opposition in Fleetwood awaited the winner, and a fanbase starved of trophies began to look ahead - albeit, for some, through covered eyes. Then, in the build-up to the match, it was revealed Jack Grealish had been dropped from the squad over what is understood to have been an unauthorised absence from training. The unwanted headline threatened to derail preparations for the latest round of a competition that perhaps offers Everton's best chance of winning a trophy for the first time in 31 years. Instead, the club's younger players came to the fore, led by the influential Hayden Hackney. A £16.5m summer signing from Middlesbrough, the 24-year-old made light of his inexperience at the highest level against a strong Newcastle XI, assisting James Garner's opening goal before scoring Everton's second with a close-range volley. Hackney, though, has needed to be patient early in his Everton career. After starting the opening game of the season - a 2-0 win against Crystal Palace - his only subsequent start prior to Thursday's cup victory was in the third round of the same competition against Wolves. The central midfielder is not known for being prolific - the fourth-round win was only the second time in his career he had scored and assisted in the same game - but he knitted together phases of possession and carried the ball with the confidence that led to him being named Championship player of the year last season. David Moyes, though, is a demanding manager and one perfectly prepared to keep young feet on the ground. "I thought there were bits of his game that were very good," said the Everton boss. "Getting a goal was great. There were other bits where I didn't think it was where it was [supposed to be]. "But I see this as a bit of bringing in Championship players, getting them used to the Premier League. A couple of times he got caught on the ball. "But I really enjoyed bits. He gave us a bit of an attacking play, getting into the box, and obviously getting the goal was really good. A really good assist from Thierno Barry as well, to be fair." While Hackney was ably assisted by strong performances from Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in Everton's midfield, the threadbare nature of the Toffees' squad means the development and contribution of the club's younger players could prove crucial in any success this season. Of the 10 players signed on permanent deals since Moyes rejoined the club in January 2025, seven are aged 24 or under, including Barry.
