item.content:encoded: Players aged 24 or under are playing a higher proportion of minutes for Everton this season [Getty Images] As Everton prepared to face Newcastle in the fourth round of the EFL Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, the stakes were high. A quarter-final tie against League Two opposition in Fleetwood awaited the winner, and a fanbase starved of trophies began to look ahead - albeit, for some, through covered eyes. Then, in the build-up to the match, it was revealed Jack Grealish had been dropped from the squad over what is understood to have been an unauthorised absence from training. The unwanted headline threatened to derail preparations for the latest round of a competition that perhaps offers Everton's best chance of winning a trophy for the first time in 31 years. Instead, the club's younger players came to the fore, led by the influential Hayden Hackney. A £16.5m summer signing from Middlesbrough, the 24-year-old made light of his inexperience at the highest level against a strong Newcastle XI, assisting James Garner's opening goal before scoring Everton's second with a close-range volley. Hackney, though, has needed to be patient early in his Everton career. After starting the opening game of the season - a 2-0 win against Crystal Palace - his only subsequent start prior to Thursday's cup victory was in the third round of the same competition against Wolves. The central midfielder is not known for being prolific - the fourth-round win was only the second time in his career he had scored and assisted in the same game - but he knitted together phases of possession and carried the ball with the confidence that led to him being named Championship player of the year last season. David Moyes, though, is a demanding manager and one perfectly prepared to keep young feet on the ground. "I thought there were bits of his game that were very good," said the Everton boss. "Getting a goal was great. There were other bits where I didn't think it was where it was [supposed to be]. "But I see this as a bit of bringing in Championship players, getting them used to the Premier League. A couple of times he got caught on the ball. "But I really enjoyed bits. He gave us a bit of an attacking play, getting into the box, and obviously getting the goal was really good. A really good assist from Thierno Barry as well, to be fair." While Hackney was ably assisted by strong performances from Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in Everton's midfield, the threadbare nature of the Toffees' squad means the development and contribution of the club's younger players could prove crucial in any success this season. Of the 10 players signed on permanent deals since Moyes rejoined the club in January 2025, seven are aged 24 or under, including Barry. The France Under-21 international is playing just a third season in a top-five European league after joining from Villarreal in July 2025, but his introduction to elite football has been more pressurised because of Everton's lack of options up front. Barry is the club's only specialist centre-forward, starting every match and playing 918 minutes this season. His tally of seven goals is already just one off his total from last season, despite playing 30 fewer matches. Everton have recorded 24 big chances, and Barry has been involved in 15 of them (62.5%). Whiles Moyes' hand has been somewhat forced in giving Barry game time because of a lack of alternatives, there has been a broader indication he is more prepared to back the younger members of his squad this season. The average age of Everton's starting XI in the Premier League has dropped by almost 18 months this season to 26 years and 216 days. The departure of veteran midfielder Idrissa Gueye has made a difference but first-team players aged 24 or under are playing a much higher proportion of Premier League minutes than in the previous campaign. Moyes used just 22 players in the Premier League last season. He has already used 22 in this one. Even the youngest players in the squad appear to have gained more trust. In 2025-26, players aged 21 or under totalled 1,088 minutes for the Toffees, a figure that has already been exceeded this season (1,206). At 19, Harrison Armstrong is the youngest regular in Everton's senior squad. In January, he had completed a six-month loan spell at Preston and Moyes considered sending him back to Deepdale for the remainder of last season before slowly integrating him into the first team. This season, the teenager has started every Premier League match. Winger Tyler Dibling, 20, initially struggled after a £35m move from Southampton in the summer of 2025 but was positive in getting Everton on to the front foot on against Newcastle on Thursday night. Tyrique George joined on a permanent deal from Chelsea in the summer after spending the second half of last season on loan at Everton during which he made only one league start. The 20-year-old has already made five this season, scoring his first goal for the club in the 2-2 draw with Manchester United in September. George also started the EFL Cup fixture last week and won back possession for the opening goal. Merlin Rohl broke into the team towards the end of last season and the 24-year-old midfielder, who also signed permanently in the summer following an initial loan spell, has since been trusted to fill Everton's problem position of right-back. After missing four games because of injury, he was immediately brought back into the starting XI against Chelsea. He was then preferred to the more experienced Ainsley Maitland-Niles at right-back for matches against Arsenal and Newcastle. When asked if Grealish would return to the squad for Monday's rematch at St James' Park, Moyes said he would not reveal any team news, though there is no doubt that experience still counts among the 63-year-old's most valuable commodities. Defender James Tarkowksi, 33, has been a standout performer so far this season, while the form of fellow senior players such as Jordan Pickford, 32, and Dewsbury-Hall, 28 remain critical to this Everton side. But when Everton meet Newcastle for the second time in less than a week on Monday, Grealish could again miss out. In his absence, younger heads were good enough to win a cup tie. It would be further indication of their growing influence if they were to repeat that result in the Premier League. item.title: Evan Turner has just one thing to say about Giannis Antetokounmpo after watching Cooper Flagg
item.description: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images Evan Turner has made a bold statement about Giannis Antetokounmpo after Cooper Flagg’s brilliant start to his second season. The Dallas Mavericks teenager was brilliant in the last campaign and deservedly won the Rookie of the Year award. This season, he has taken his game to the next level. That has led to a lot of praise from many big names in the game, but the boldest one may have just come from Turner. Evan Turner says Cooper Flagg is better than Giannis Antetokounmpo Flagg’s Mavericks and Antetokounmpo’s Heat faced each other recently, and the two players put on a show. Both of them scored 29 points and recorded 11 assists for their respective sides, but Dallas edged the game by four points in the end. Antetokounmpo is regarded by many as one of the best in the game, but Turner believes Flagg looked even better than him, despite being nearly half his age. Speaking on the Open Floor NBA Talk show , the former 76ers guard said: “Hey, I was sceptical, bro, but Cooper… He could have had 40-something. He literally was getting his guys in like that. Hey, that’s a bad boy, bro. “When I saw it, I said, man, he is better than Giannis. And Giannis is in old-school attack mode. And Cooper was on some chill ‘I know how to win’ type. Like, did you feel that? He was almost like: ‘Wait, I know how to win.’ “He literally turned it on, and he was going at Wiggins, then taking it into the paint on Giannis. Like, he was being nice that night. He should have had a 40-point triple. That boy is cold. He’s here.” Turner concluded by saying: “It looked like, correct me if I’m wrong, it looked like he was hooping with his little bros. Like, it looked like he was hooping on a smaller rim.” Flagg really is a superstar in the making, but he still has a lot to learn and achieve before he can be spoken about in the same breath as Antetokounmpo. However, early signs really are positive, and Dallas Mavericks fans have every reason to be excited about their young prodigy. item.title: Rams’ Sean McVay laughs off Aaron Donald’s fumble recovery fail vs. Chargers
item.description: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Rams’ Sean McVay laughs off Aaron Donald’s fumble recovery fail vs. Chargers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams cruised past the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday , but Sean McVay could not resist poking a little fun at Aaron Donald for one play that got away from the future Hall of Famer. Late in the third quarter of the Rams’ 24-9 win at SoFi Stadium, undrafted rookie linebacker Wesley Bailey strip-sacked Justin Herbert at the Chargers’ 26-yard line. The loose ball bounced right toward Donald, giving him a chance at a scoop-and-score. Instead, the 35-year-old tried to scoop it up near the 20 and whiffed. He stumbled, fell on the ball and knocked it out of bounds, allowing the Chargers to keep possession after a 9-yard loss. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) McVay was all smiles when asked about the play after the game. “Oh man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that,” McVay said, via Adam Grosbard of the Los Angeles Daily News. “He couldn’t even look at me. At least we can laugh about it right now.” The Rams head coach also told radio play-by-play voice J.B. Long that he was going to “crush him” for the missed opportunity. It would have been a special moment for Donald, who has never scored a touchdown in his NFL career. The three-time Defensive Player of the Year retired in March 2024 after 10 seasons, only to come back this summer on a one-year, $20 million deal . His return made the Rams’ defensive front even scarier alongside Myles Garrett , whom Los Angeles acquired from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason. Donald has still made his share of plays this season. In the Rams’ Week 5 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, he fell on a fumble forced by Nate Landman to give Los Angeles the ball with a chance to win. The miss did not cost the Rams on Sunday. Los Angeles held the Chargers scoreless after halftime, intercepted Herbert twice and dropped the Chargers to 0-7 for the first time since Jim Harbaugh was their quarterback . The Rams improved to 4-4 with their second straight win. Donald will look for another chance at his first career touchdown when the Rams visit the Washington Commanders next Sunday. Related: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns Related: Puka Nacua issues demand to Rams’ offense after Week 8 win vs. Chargers

item.title: ‘Coming Together And Working Hard’ – How Christian Lee Is Paving The Way For Hawaii’s Next Generation Of Fighters
item.description: Christian “The Warrior” Lee has reached the absolute pinnacle of mixed martial arts. Now, the two-division ONE World Champion is actively laying the foundation for a new generation of Hawaiian athletes to do the same. The 28-year-old began his martial arts journey as a teenage debutant and today reigns supreme over both the lightweight and welterweight MMA divisions. Away from the global spotlight, a deeply personal chapter continues to grow: he and his wife, Katie, recently welcomed their fourth child into the world. View this post on Instagram Before his story continues, a massive assignment in Bangkok’s iconic Lumpinee Stadium awaits. Lee will defend his lightweight MMA gold against ONE Welterweight Submission Grappling World Champion Tye Ruotolo in the main event of The Inner Circle 37 on Friday, November 6. The Asia primetime blockbuster will be exclusively available to subscribers at live.onefc.com . While the global fan base sees the heavy gold wrapped around his waist, fewer witness the grueling early mornings dedicated to helping eager local students dare to dream bigger. Building A Home For Local Talent Christian Lee co-owns Prodigy Training Center in Waipahu, Hawaii, alongside his wife. The family gym, which he formally rebranded in 2024, has rapidly evolved into a vital rallying point for martial artists across the island. Named in loving tribute to his late sister, the facility is built entirely around lifting others up. “The Warrior” coaches students of every skill level on those mats, partnering with his younger brother, Adrian “The Phenom” Lee , to bring the elite techniques they hone in global competition directly back to their community. Lee told onefc.com: “The gym’s doing great. We’ve had a lot of guys competing, and a lot of guys winning their fights, too. We’re just building up a strong community, those who just enjoy training and enjoy martial arts. “We’ve got a strong youth team, and we’re getting some kids ready to start their amateur youth MMA careers. We’re bringing them overseas to California next year. So, yeah, it’s been great.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship That grassroots guidance extends far beyond the amateur ranks. Lee is actively helping fellow athletes make the difficult leap to the professional circuit, and virtually no one is better positioned to show them the way. At just 20 years old, he became the youngest-ever male MMA World Champion when he dethroned Shinya “Tobikan Judan” Aoki for the lightweight gold in May 2019. Seven years later, he is paying that invaluable experience forward, guiding Hawaii’s next wave of fighters toward the exact dreams he once chased himself. He continued: “We had a few amateur fighters. One of my guys just fought in the California amateur show. He won. Another one of my guys just fought; he had a pro match in the States, and he won his third MMA match. So we have a few rising pros, and a few amateurs that are getting ready to turn pro as well.” View this post on Instagram Givi

Now, the two-division ONE World Champion is actively laying the foundation for a new generation of Hawaiian athletes to do the same. The 28-year-old began his martial arts journey as a teenage debutant and today reigns supreme over both the lightweight and welterweight MMA divisions. Away from the global spotlight, a deeply personal chapter continues to grow: he and his wife, Katie, recently welcomed their fourth child into the world. View this post on Instagram Before his story continues, a massive assignment in Bangkok’s iconic Lumpinee Stadium awaits. Lee will defend his lightweight MMA gold against ONE Welterweight Submission Grappling World Champion Tye Ruotolo in the main event of The Inner Circle 37 on Friday, November 6. The Asia primetime blockbuster will be exclusively available to subscribers at live.onefc.com . While the global fan base sees the heavy gold wrapped around his waist, fewer witness the grueling early mornings dedicated to helping eager local students dare to dream bigger. Building A Home For Local Talent Christian Lee co-owns Prodigy Training Center in Waipahu, Hawaii, alongside his wife. The family gym, which he formally rebranded in 2024, has rapidly evolved into a vital rallying point for martial artists across the island. Named in loving tribute to his late sister, the facility is built entirely around lifting others up. “The Warrior” coaches students of every skill level on those mats, partnering with his younger brother, Adrian “The Phenom” Lee , to bring the elite techniques they hone in global competition directly back to their community. Lee told onefc.com: “The gym’s doing great. We’ve had a lot of guys competing, and a lot of guys winning their fights, too. We’re just building up a strong community, those who just enjoy training and enjoy martial arts. “We’ve got a strong youth team, and we’re getting some kids ready to start their amateur youth MMA careers. We’re bringing them overseas to California next year. So, yeah, it’s been great.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship That grassroots guidance extends far beyond the amateur ranks. Lee is actively helping fellow athletes make the difficult leap to the professional circuit, and virtually no one is better positioned to show them the way. At just 20 years old, he became the youngest-ever male MMA World Champion when he dethroned Shinya “Tobikan Judan” Aoki for the lightweight gold in May 2019. Seven years later, he is paying that invaluable experience forward, guiding Hawaii’s next wave of fighters toward the exact dreams he once chased himself. He continued: “We had a few amateur fighters. One of my guys just fought in the California amateur show. He won. Another one of my guys just fought; he had a pro match in the States, and he won his third MMA match. So we have a few rising pros, and a few amateurs that are getting ready to turn pro as well.” View this post on Instagram Giving An Island Its Stage Christian Lee understands that geographic distance can often serve as a Hawaiian fighter’s toughest opponent. Oahu sits roughly 2,400 miles from San Francisco, one of the closest points on the U.S. mainland, requiring nearly six hours in the air to reach any major hub. For a young athlete, every chance to prove themselves is a very long, expensive trip away. With no active amateur MMA promotions left on the island, Lee decided to fill the glaring void himself, cultivating opportunities in the very place where his family’s renowned fighting legacy originally took root. The two-division MMA World Champion shared: “We just held an event in our gym, and we call it a smoker event. Basically, we hold fights in our gym – no winner, no loser – but we get to see who the better fighter is, and we encourage our guys to go for the finish. So we matchmade a whole card. “We had, like, 15 matches, MMA and kickboxing, and we had 10 of our guys from our gym competing in that, and most of them all won their matches, so it was a great event. We had like 400 people in the gym watching.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship The heavy cost of that geographic gap becomes obvious when the island’s raw talents are forced to leave. According to Lee, many aspiring pros head to places like Las Vegas in search of resources. The homegrown athletes who do fly out often face opponents holding vastly more experience, simply because mainland athletes can easily drive from state to state picking up fights every weekend. Lee’s in-house events are his direct method of leveling those odds. For a hungry up-and-comer, a packed night competing inside Prodigy Training Center is much more than practice. It is tangible proof that someone believes they belong in the sport. “The Warrior” added: “These guys train really hard, but there’s no promotion. So we do these types of events so that they can get the fighting experience they need, and then travel overseas from Hawaii, and then they’ll be ready. I’m happy that we’re able to play a part in that. “It’s some work, it definitely is, especially with this fight coming up. I definitely had a lot to think about, but it was a great event, the turnout was great, and I’m happy to do that because in Hawaii, there’s no platform for all of the guys on the island to fight.” View this post on Instagram A Culture Worth Fighting For Christian Lee has seen firsthand that the island’s deep-rooted hunger to compete never faded. Across Hawaii, athletes fiercely love to train in MMA, kickboxing, boxing, wrestling, and grappling. He sees a local scene desperate for a larger stage. The Prodigy Training Center head honcho grew up immersed in that exact culture, and he remembers precisely what steady competition meant to his own development as a teenager. Now, “The Warrior” is determined to provide the next generation of local hopefuls with a similar launching pad. Lee said: “When I was 15, I was able to fight three times a month. And now these guys who are wanting to fight, I see that there’s definitely a need for it. So I’m happy that we can put on events like this. And when we have like 30 guys competing, they’re all in the gym, and there’s not a single altercation in the gym. “It’s great to see everyone coming together from different gyms, and just being happy to have that platform to fight, to get where they want to go. A lot of these guys, really, their dream is to be pro fighters.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship No significant movement is ever carried by just one person, and Lee keeps elite company. His younger brother coaches directly alongside him, and his wife, Katie, ensures the business operations run seamlessly. Beyond the immediate gym walls, the island’s absolute best have joined the cause, including multi-time MMA World Champion Max Holloway. The 28-year-old reflected: “We’ve been blessed to have a lot of support from my friends over the years. Max has been coming in regularly to train and to help give me looks in the room. And another good friend, Ray Cooper, has been coming in, too. “Between the three of us – me, Max, and Ray – we’re like the seasoned fighters coming out of Hawaii who still live and train out of Hawaii. Despite all of the odds against us out here, we’re still just putting in the work and not feeling a need to leave the island. We’re just coming together and working hard. I’m happy with everything.” View this post on Instagram Source

item.title: The four factors that make Brighton genuine Premier League title contenders
item.description: When Fabian Hurzeler was asked about Brighton’s possible participation in the title race, he tended to invoke Getafe in his answer. And if a club from Madrid are not exactly an opponent in the Premier League, this was Hurzeler’s version of an old cliché. He is taking it one game at a time, and Brighton & Hove Albion ’s next game is against Getafe in the Europa Conference League . More pertinently, though, their last one was away at Manchester City . They defeated the league leaders . Brighton’s last week has served as a barometer of their status against the established powers. They played well against Liverpool at Anfield, but lost 2-0. They twice led against City in the Carabao Cup, but went out on penalties. They beat them in the Premier League. For a club with plenty of high-profile scalps in recent years, the Etihad Stadium was the final frontier. They had won everywhere else of note. Now Hurzeler could maintain the pretence that the only thing on his mind was Getafe. Brighton triumphed in Manchester in another impressive result for Fabian Hurzeler’s side (Getty) The unlikely challengers can deflect attention by citing the concerns they would have in other seasons. Eleven years ago, as Leicester City were an unexpected presence near the top of the table, Claudio Ranieri used to talk about targeting 40 points, even when it was clear Leicester would reach the usual barrier for safety with months to spare. Now Brighton are already halfway to the other mythical number, 38. Ranieri’s rhetoric was such that he could switch to meaningless but entertaining catchphrases; Hurzeler’s is less likely to spend spring saying “dilly ding, dilly dong”. But the subject of a title tilt could become inescapable if Brighton extend their superb start. That seems possible: they have played the rest of the current top five and do not face any again until the return game with City in January. They don’t see Chelsea again until April, Liverpool or Arsenal until the final two games. Leicester showed that an unlikely title triumph can be pulled off (PA Wire) Is there a title decider there? History would suggest not. Brighton have never finished in the top five of the top flight. They often start seasons well – they had 21 points after 12 games in 2024-25, 13 after six in 2022-23, 12 after five in 2021-22 – but have a past of winless spells, too: under Hurzeler, they twice went six league matches without victory last season. History suggests, too, that if Brighton are to upset the odds, it does not just depend upon their results. item.content:encoded: When Fabian Hurzeler was asked about Brighton’s possible participation in the title race, he tended to invoke Getafe in his answer. And if a club from Madrid are not exactly an opponent in the Premier League, this was Hurzeler’s version of an old cliché. He is taking it one game at a time, and Brighton & Hove Albion ’s next game is against Getafe in the Europa Conference League . More pertinently, though, their last one was away at Manchester City . They defeated the league leaders . Brighton’s last week has served as a barometer of their status against the established powers. They played well against Liverpool at Anfield, but lost 2-0. They twice led against City in the Carabao Cup, but went out on penalties. They beat them in the Premier League. For a club with plenty of high-profile scalps in recent years, the Etihad Stadium was the final frontier. They had won everywhere else of note. Now Hurzeler could maintain the pretence that the only thing on his mind was Getafe. Brighton triumphed in Manchester in another impressive result for Fabian Hurzeler’s side (Getty) The unlikely challengers can deflect attention by citing the concerns they would have in other seasons. Eleven years ago, as Leicester City were an unexpected presence near the top of the table, Claudio Ranieri used to talk about targeting 40 points, even when it was clear Leicester would reach the usual barrier for safety with months to spare. Now Brighton are already halfway to the other mythical number, 38. Ranieri’s rhetoric was such that he could switch to meaningless but entertaining catchphrases; Hurzeler’s is less likely to spend spring saying “dilly ding, dilly dong”. But the subject of a title tilt could become inescapable if Brighton extend their superb start. That seems possible: they have played the rest of the current top five and do not face any again until the return game with City in January. They don’t see Chelsea again until April, Liverpool or Arsenal until the final two games. Leicester showed that an unlikely title triumph can be pulled off (PA Wire) Is there a title decider there? History would suggest not. Brighton have never finished in the top five of the top flight. They often start seasons well – they had 21 points after 12 games in 2024-25, 13 after six in 2022-23, 12 after five in 2021-22 – but have a past of winless spells, too: under Hurzeler, they twice went six league matches without victory last season. History suggests, too, that if Brighton are to upset the odds, it does not just depend upon their results. When Leicester were champions in 2016, it was facilitated by the failures of others, as no one else secured more than 71 points. Ranieri’s team earned 81. Now some of the supposed superpowers, Manchester United in particular, seem to be taking themselves out of contention. A sizeable punishment could rule City out. It is altogether harder to see Arsenal, in particular, from ending up with under 80 points. Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has built an excellent squad despite heavy turnover (PA Wire) Some elements indicate that Brighton should be taken seriously. One, oddly, lies in a couple of defeats: by losing their final two games of last season, they missed out on a Europa League spot. But the lighter load of the Conference League – both in its fixture list and lesser opponents – could equip them better for the Premier League. Another lies in the firepower of Hurzeler’s team. Brighton are the top scorers in the division. They are expert at sharing the goals around: 16 players have found the net in all competitions, 11 of them in the Premier League. It is all the more remarkable as they have been without last season’s first-choice front three, with Danny Welbeck gone to Chelsea and Yankuba Minteh and Kaoru Mitoma yet to play in the top flight this season. With Minteh fit again and the prospect of Mitoma being back next month, Brighton could have more devastating wingers. Brighton’s strong start has come despite being without last year’s front three (Getty) They have impressed defensively. They conceded four times to Chelsea, but only three other goals. Shutting City out gave them a sixth clean sheet of the season already, while they have only been breached once at home. Luka Vuskovic has been outstanding, submitting an early application for the title of signing of the season. But a test for players being introduced to such a physical and demanding division as the Croatian defender and the 21-year-old midfielder Chema Andres is whether they can sustain that form for a whole campaign. The same question can be applied to the team as a whole and to veterans like Pascal Gross and Lewis Dunk. There are alternatives to each. The seeming strength of Brighton’s squad counts in their favour, even if it depends on Hurzeler continuing to pick the right option at the right time. Squad management will be key for Fabian Hurzeler and Brighton (Getty) But certainly, with Brighton already five points clear of sixth place and seven ahead of seventh, they are unlikely to get a better chance to qualify for the Champions League. Yet as they continue to be an indictment of the elite, selling their best players at premium prices, replacing them, and continuing to prosper, they are indulging in a unique experiment . Can a selling club win the world’s richest league? We may find out in May.

item.title: NFL Week 8 INSTANT reactions: Are the Cowboys cooked? Ravens need to make a move
item.description: Subscribe to Football 301 with Nate Tice Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube Nate Tice & Hayden Winks dive into their instant takeaways from Week 8 of NFL action. The duo start with their takeaways from a sloppy Sunday night win for the Washington Commanders over the reeling Philadelphia Eagles. Nate & Hayden move on to their Pick 6 takeaways, featuring the Cincinnati Bengals winning a shootout with the Tennessee Titans, the Denver Broncos taking the AFC West lead over the Kansas City Chiefs, the Arizona Cardinals upsetting the Dallas Cowboys, the Detroit Lions beating the undefeated Minnesota Vikings, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beating the Atlanta Falcons without throwing a pass and the Pittsburgh Steelers shutting down the Cleveland Browns. The duo wrap up with a few Extra Credit items, including Lamar Jackson’s thumb injury and whether the Baltimore Ravens need to make a move for a quarterback, the Las Vegas Raiders & New York Jets lighting it up in a barn burner and the Jacksonville Jaguars crushing the Indianapolis Colts. item.title: Predators’ Chris MacFarland breaks silence on Shane Wright trade
item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Predators’ Chris MacFarland breaks silence on Shane Wright trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Nashville Predators acquired Shane Wright in a trade with the Seattle Kraken on Sunday. This ends a bit of a saga within the Kraken. Wright has preferred a trade out of Seattle for a while now. He finally got his wish with this move. The newest Predators forward has had a rollercoaster of a career to this point. He was never able to establish himself as part of the Kraken’s core group of forwards. Nashville is excited to get a chance to work with him , as general manager Chris MacFarland explained on Sunday. “We are excited to add Shane to our mix of forwards,” the Predators GM said, via NHL.com. “We feel he will bring a strong, two-way game to our team and will add to the pace of our lineup… Shane will continue to grow as a player, and we look forward to working with him.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Wright played nearly 170 games with Seattle prior to this trade. He scored 39 goals and 82 points in that time. The former fourth overall pick only has four points in 14 games this season. In return for Wright, the Predators sent young winger Matthew Wood to the Kraken. Wood, a former first-round pick, had just three points this season through 14 games. The 21-year-old scored 17 goals and 30 points during his first full NHL season in 2025-26. Wright finally has the fresh start he has sought for some time. What sort of impact he brings remains to be seen, but a fresh start inherently brings a new opportunity to thrive. The Predators return to the ice on Tuesday when they take on the Carolina Hurricanes. Related: Kraken, Predators swap forwards in intriguing midseason trade Related: Predators’ Barry Trotz drops Alex Ovechkin truth bomb amid final game in Nashville

item.title: Why Browns’ Todd Monken didn’t bench Deshaun Watson while Steelers teed off on him for 8 sacks in blowout
item.description: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images Why Browns’ Todd Monken didn’t bench Deshaun Watson while Steelers teed off on him for 8 sacks in blowout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns endured a brutal afternoon against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Todd Monken’s decision to keep Deshaun Watson under center, though, revealed something about his approach to developing the offense. Despite watching his quarterback absorb eight sacks in Sunday’s embarrassing 27-6 defeat , the first-year head coach never seriously considered pulling him. Rather than turning to Shedeur Sanders, Monken wanted Watson to battle through adversity . Monken also accepted responsibility for the offensive breakdown. Through the first eight weeks of the 2026 NFL season, the Cleveland Browns have lived on a chaotic, razor-thin edge under first-year head coach Todd Monken . They have now compiled a 5-3 record that has showcased both incredible late-game resilience and glaring structural vulnerabilities. After bottoming out in a demoralizing 34-10 opening-day blowout in Jacksonville, Cleveland vaulted into playoff contention with five fourth-quarter comeback victories. Those were headlined by three walk-off field goals from Andre Szmyt against Pittsburgh, Baltimore, and Tennessee. However, their magic met a harsh reality check in Week 8 at Acrisure Stadium. This loss dropped Cleveland behind Pittsburgh in the AFC North. #Browns Todd Monken never considered taking Deshaun Watson out when the #Steelers were teeing off on him in the second half: pic.twitter.com/v9R6dqEzOd Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) November 1, 2026 According to Scott Petrak of The Chronicle-Telegram, Monken wanted Watson to accumulate more playing experience rather than remove him following the mounting pressure. “I want to see him play. I want to see him continue to play and battle,” Monken explained. item.title: Andy Reid Makes Muted Statement on Kingsley Suamataia After Second Benching
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs looks on in the second quarter of a game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) Getty ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 02: Kingsley Suamataia #76 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs off the field after being injured during the fourth quarter in the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs made a surprise decision prior to the team’s loss against the Denver Broncos on Sunday in benching left guard Kingsley Suamataia. The 2024 second round pick had already been benched in Week 4 in the win against the Las Vegas Raiders for unspecified reasons, and ahead of the team’s bout in Week 8 he did the very same thing. Andy Reid Comments on Kingsley Suamataia’s Benching Speaking to the media after the game, Reid declined to answer why he benched the third year offensive lineman. Andy Reid on Kingsley Suamataia: “It’s just between Kingsley and I.” — Nate Taylor (@ByNateTaylor) November 2, 2026 “It’s just between Kingsley and I,” Reid said after the loss when asked for the reasoning behind the decision. Kingsley Suamataia Second Benching Points to Ongoing Issues Getty ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 02: Kingsley Suamataia #76 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs off the field after being injured during the fourth quarter in the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. item.title: Athletic end Real Sociedad’s four-game league run as visitors protest Berenguer penalty
item.description: Athletic end Real Sociedad’s four-game league run as visitors protest Berenguer penalty Athletic Club beat Real Sociedad 2-1 at San Mamés on Sunday 1 November to end their rivals' run of four straight league wins. The visitors have formally disputed the first-half penalty that decided the derby, while Athletic lost another striker to injury. Every goal in the Bilbao derby arrived before half-time. Nico Williams provided the assist for the opening goal. Luka Sučić equalised on the half-hour. A crowd of 50,092 watched the game. Before kick-off, Unai Simón presented his Yashin Trophy to the home crowd. A minute’s silence was also held for the victims of the Urda rail accident. Real Sociedad dispute the penalty that settled the derby The visitors left Bilbao angry about the decisive spot-kick. In its official match report, Real Sociedad called it a penalty that never was and criticised VAR for not stepping in. The club statement added that the chip inside the match ball shows Jon Aramburu made contact with the ball in his challenge on Nico Williams. Pellegrino Matarazzo said that for him it was clearly not a penalty. The Real Sociedad coach could not understand why VAR had not intervened to cancel it. He was booked for dissent in the 65th minute, a minute after Mamadou Sarr received a yellow card for the same offence. Referee Alejandro Hernandez showed Real Sociedad four yellow cards in total, against two for Athletic. The statistics point in two directions. Real Sociedad dominated the ball, completing 514 accurate passes to Athletic’s 307. Terzić’s side created the clearer chances, however. Unai Simón made four saves, while Álex Remiro made one. Sučić was the highest-rated player on the pitch at 7.52. Athletic win but lose another striker The victory came at a cost. Maroan Sannadi felt his hamstring early in the game. Athletic will need one or two more days to know how long he will be out. His injury follows Gorka Guruzeta’s serious knee injury at Valencia on 17 October, which left the squad short of strikers. With 83 minutes on the pitch, Navarro created four key passes and was rated 7.2. The win was Athletic’s third in a row across all competitions, after a 6-1 victory over Prat and a 4-0 win against Getafe. They sit seventh, two points behind Sevilla. Real Betis are four points clear of Real Sociedad. Athletic also have a game in hand. Their matchday-eight fixture at Rayo Vallecano was suspended. Objects landed on the field during that game, among them paper planes and tiny balls made of silicone. Rayo were fined €6,000, the maximum sanction under the disciplinary code. The match will resume behind closed doors at Vallecas on Wednesday 9 December at 20:00. Real Sociedad return to action first, hosting Lyon in the Europa League league phase on Thursday 5 November. item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Tyrone Tracy Jr. #29 of the New York Giants carries the ball defended by Cooper DeJean #33 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the fourth quarter in the game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles have lost six games in a row and the losing streak might continue next weekend. The Birds are three-point home underdogs to the New York Giants, according to FanDuel . As a reminder, the Eagles have NEVER won as home underdogs since Nick Sirianni was hired as head coach in 2021. They are 0-8 in those situations. Go Birds! Join Eagles fans on the SB Nation app! Share every touchdown celebration, big defensive stop and passionate game-day opinion with fellow Eagles fans. Join our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Jump easily between communities and conversations Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Eagles have longed owned the G-Men. But that might be changing. The Giants currently lead the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record. And that’s despite the fact they lost their starting quarterback, Jaxson Dart, to a season-ending injury in Week 2. J.J. McCarthy is showing some promise with the Giants after previously being a bust for the Minnesota Vikings. John Harbaugh is going to have his team fired up to take on a reeling Eagles squad. The Giants also have a rest advantage in this matchup since they’re coming off their Week 8 bye while the Eagles are coming off a Sunday night road game. The Eagles aren’t inspiring any confidence at the moment. It’s impossible to give them the benefit of the doubt. What say you?

item.title: Julian Erosa Explains Retiring From UFC
item.description: Julian Erosa UFC Getty Long-time UFC featherweight fan favorite Julian Erosa explained why he made the decision to retire from mixed martial arts. Erosa laid down his gloves in the center of the Octagon following his first-round KO win over JeongYeong Lee at UFC Vegas 123, as he officially retired from the UFC with a final record of 10-9 inside the Octagon. Erosa had already announced before the fight that he was going to retire, so it wasn’t a surprise to see him hang up his gloves despite a terrific performance against Lee. So, why is Erosa retiring when he is seemingly still a UFC-caliber fighter? Julian Erosa Breaks Down Retirement Decision Speaking to reporters after UFC Vegas 123, Erosa broke down his decision to retire from MMA. “I was going back and forth in my mind: If I win the fight, I’m going to want to do it again because it’s the best feeling in the world. If I lose the fight, I’m going to want redemption. Win, lose or draw, I’m going to want to come back in here. So before I even got the fight, I told my wife, ‘This is going to be the last one,’ and be content with that decision. Once I was at ease with it and at peace with that decision, I could just go in the fight and just focus on it being a fight just like any other fight camp – focus on that and then be, I’m already happy with the decision of retiring. I didn’t want to be the guy that’s going to retire and then come back in a month. I’m happy with the way it turned out. I haven’t left any stone unturned. I made it from ‘Ultimate Fighter’ to Contender Series, been cut and rehired by the UFC so many times – I want to go out on my own terms,” Erosa said (via MMAjunkie.com ). Will Julian Erosa Compete Again? While Erosa did announce his retirement, it’s hard to take MMA fighters’ retirements at face value sometimes, as so many of them have hung up their gloves just to return a few years later. In Erosa’s case, it does feel like he’s done for good, as he has a young family to spend his time with. Not only that, but he was knocked out eight times in his career, so it is a smart decision to stop getting hit in the head anymore. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Julian Erosa Explains Retiring From UFC appeared first on HEAVY .

Keys to Bears vs. Seahawks matchup The Eagles need all the help they can get on the scoring front. Lineman Lane Johnson made the decision to retire earlier this season, leaving a big hole in the offensive line. Jalen Hurts is also out for the entire season after sustaining blood clots in his lungs. Saquon Barkley is available to play, but he isn’t fully healthy as he recovers from his own injury. Tanner McKee stands out as the starter, completing 49 out of 80 passes for 426 yards and two touchdowns and one interception after two games. Barkley leads the run game with 43 carries for 244 yards and one touchdown while catching six passes for 17 yards. DeVonta Smith leads receivers with 26 receptions for 310 yards and two touchdowns. DonTayvion Wicks follows with 19 catches for 284 yards and a touchdown, while Makai Lemon has 25 receptions for 194 yards and a touchdown. Sonny Styles leads that side of the ball with 46 tackles, four pass deflections, three TFL, one sack, one forced fumble, and one interception. item.title: Cowboys Could Cash Out on George Pickens ‘Subscription’ With Trade
item.description: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Of all the things that have gone wrong with the Dallas Cowboys thus far in what appears to be another cursed NFL season, the steady disappearance of wide receiver George Pickens is low down on the list. But that’s not because it’s unworthy of attention or scrutiny–it’s just because there are so many other issues to consider, so many other failures to address. The defense, the coaching, the indecisive approach to personnel, it all adds up to an incredibly disappointing 2026 season that started with the Cowboys openly talking about a trip to the Super Bowl, a bit of bravado that looks ridiculous in hindsight, like a gambler buying a lottery ticket certain that the millions are coming soon. It’s easy to lose Pickens in that shuffle. On Sunday, in the dramatic 33-30 loss to the Cardinals in overtime, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott targeted Pickens only four times, and Pickens played only about 40 snaps, around where he was in Week 7. A defensive meltdown was the reason the Cowboys collapsed on Sunday, but it is impossible to ignore the fact that the Cowboys are, well, ignoring Pickens. Cowboys Cutting George Pickens Snaps Why that’s happening is a fair question. Last week, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer publicly called out Pickens for his lack of seriousness when it comes to blocking in the run game. Pickens saw his snaps drop thereafter. But this is the same receiver who posted 93 catches and 1,429 yards last year, who was hailed for having the best training camp of any player on the Cowboys roster, and who was clearly focused on a big season that would lead to a big payout in free agency next winter. None of it has happened. The Cowboys have Pickens, and they’re not using him. Cleverly, Dallas Morning News writer Joseph Hoyt compared Pickens to, “a subscription that the Cowboys forgot they signed up for.” And Hoyt writes that the Cowboys, who have Pickens on a one-year, $27 million franchise tag contract, should dump Pickens and pick up whatever draft asset they can. The Cowboys treat George Pickens like a subscription they forgot they signed up for.It’s time to consider trading him before the deadline.Column: https://t.co/jYLODqtfql pic.twitter.com/mZqsCx9pxd — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) November 2, 2026 Trade Now, or Trade Later The Cowboys-George Pickens marriage clearly is not working. Hoyt suggests they should recognize that and explore what cashing out might bring. He wrote: “If the Cowboys were to trade Pickens then his new team couldn’t negotiate a long-term deal with him until after the season. That means a new team would be getting a receiver truly on an expiring contract, lowering the value of any potential midseason trade with Pickens. The Cowboys could wait until the offseason, tag Pickens again for a potential one-year deal worth more than $32 million, and then trade Pickens to a new destination … Would trading Pickens in a lost season for a Day 2 pick be worth it? That’s not where we thought this season, and relationship, was heading two months ago. item.title: What Raiders’ Klint Kubiak said about turning to Mike Washington Jr. with Ashton Jeanty in doghouse
item.description: Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images What Raiders’ Klint Kubiak said about turning to Mike Washington Jr. with Ashton Jeanty in doghouse appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Klint Kubiak and the Raiders got a much-needed win against the New York Jets in Week 8 that saw Brock Bowers set a mark not seen since 2016 . Ashton Jeanty called out the Jets before the game and was asked about his comments, taking the high road as his team turned to Mike Washington Jr. as its leading ballcarrier. Kubiak’s comments were shared by Sam Gordon of the Las Vegas Review Journal, during which he addressed the Jeanty situation. “Yeah, you know guys, that’s my call, and Ashton’s still gonna be a big part of our team. Had a huge catch, he’s gonna be a huge part of our run game going forward, and, you know, we just wanna give Mike a few more opportunities a day, and, you know, I think both guys are going to be a huge part of our rushing and passing success moving forward.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Kubiak replied “no” when asked if Jeanty’s comments on the Jets had anything to do with his lack of carries on the day. Washington Jr. did well with 25 carries for 83 yards while Jeanty was a factor in the passing game with three catches for 64 yards. QB Kirk Cousins focused on Jeanty along with tight ends Bowers and Michael Mayer in the passing game as the Raiders beat a struggling NY team. Rex Ryan called out Jeanty after his comments on the Jets, showing that the Raiders still have the ability to move the dial on a national level. Fans care about the Raiders from coast-to-coast, and Jeanty is a big reason why. He’s an exciting running back who will get another chance to shine in the near future as the Raiders’ train rolls on. Related: Raiders news: Only 1 thing surprises Klint Kubiak about Brock Bowers after another big day Related: Raiders’ Kirk Cousins breaks silence on ‘wellness celly’ after TD vs. Jets

item.title: ‘Kirk Cousins, Come Home to Minnesota’ — Ex-NFL QB Pushes Vikings to ‘Secretly’ Consider Trade for Raiders Star And Replace Kyler Murray
item.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Minnesota Vikings moved on from Kirk Cousins, traded J.J. McCarthy, and handed Kyler Murray the starting job. Now, Minnesota has a quarterback problem that makes those decisions harder to ignore. Murray has yet to give the offense the level of play it needs, while Cousins is putting together strong performances in Las Vegas, in a turn of events that has former NFL quarterback Chase Daniel wondering why the Vikings have not quietly explored bringing their former starter back. Chase Daniel Urges Vikings to Explore Kirk Cousins Trade Speaking on “Bussin’ With The Boys” after Week 8, Daniel argued that Minnesota should not rely entirely on its defense while Murray works through his uneven performances. He believes the Vikings need to consider bringing Cousins back from the Las Vegas Raiders, especially after the veteran’s recent outing against the New York Jets. “If you are the Vikings, you need to be back in the race and back in the thought of absolutely looking into Kirk Cousins. Why are you not secretly checking into the Raiders and Kirk Cousins? Kirk is absolutely balling and had an amazing game versus the Jets. Your defense cannot carry you the entire year,” Daniel said. Cousins, who ranks 10th in PFN’s NFL QB Impact Metric , has given Daniel a reason to raise the possibility. Against New York, he completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns without an interception in a 38-33 victory. He also scored a rushing touchdown, finishing with a 141.0 passer rating. His previous two appearances included 295 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams, following 313 yards and two touchdowns against Buffalo. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Daniel’s proposal also comes as Minnesota deals with the departure of J.J. McCarthy. The Vikings traded the quarterback to the New York Giants, where he has taken over in light of Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury. McCarthy’s arrival has helped New York move into first place in the NFC East, giving Minnesota another reason to reconsider its earlier quarterback decisions. “I agree that Kyler played well in the second half. And, oh, by the way, you traded away J.J. McCarthy, who’s now starting for the Giants and has the Giants in first place in the NFC East. Let that sink in right there,” Daniel remarked. item.title: 🟥 Juve-Napoli, press: Koop deserved red after 10'! Lucumi too, review 📺
item.description: 🟥 Juve-Napoli, press: Koop deserved red after 10'! Lucumi too, review 📺 Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 in Sunday's big Serie A clash between two of the biggest disappointments of the season so far. Watch every Serie BKT match live with LaB Channel on OneFootball: subscribe for just €9.99 a month! At the Allianz Stadium, superb goals from Alajbegovic and Boga , both in the second half, proved decisive after a largely uneventful opening period. Everything, however, could have changed after just ten minutes, when Koopmeiners brought down Anguissa with a nasty challenge . Even as it happened, DAZN 's co-commentator suggested VAR might intervene, but no call came. Referee Sozza then allowed play to resume without even booking the Dutchman . 😳 Newspapers in no doubt: it was a red! A wrong decision, judging by the comments in today's newspapers. Both Gazzetta dello Sport and Corriere dello Sport felt the Dutchman's foul warranted a sending-off. Gazzetta gives Sozza a rating of 4.5 , adding that " as early as the eighth minute, he fails to book McKennie. In the 11th, he doesn't even book Koopmeiners: a challenge halfway up Anguissa's leg that constitutes serious foul play, clearly dangerous — it should have been a red ". Corriere , meanwhile, rates the referee's performance a 5 : " Sozza's performance was far from spotless — quite the opposite: the opening quarter of an hour was a nightmare (even though Halloween was over), and the Koopmeiners decision hangs over the match. A late challenge, with a straight leg and studs showing: true, it wasn't a 'lunge' but a 'scrape', which gives those arguing his innocence some room for manoeuvre, but going from a possible red to not even awarding a foul (and a yellow) means an error on the pitch and confusion in his head ". For former referee Gianpaolo Calvarese , however, "a red would have been excessive . But if Sozza had shown one, I don't think VAR would have intervened". According to Corriere, there could also have been another sending-off : " Speaking of risking a red: Lucumi takes a big risk when, already on a booking, he makes a clumsy challenge on Lucca. A second yellow would have been justified ". This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇮🇹 here.

item.title: Travis Kelce Has Strong Words on Andy Reid After Chiefs’ Loss to Broncos
item.description: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce sends a clear message on head coach Andy Reid after losing to the Broncos. Getty Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce runs the ball against the Broncos in Week 8. Getty Head coach Andy Reid and Travis Kelce Getty Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce takes responsibility for his role in the team's performance over the past few weeks. Getty The Kansas City Chiefs took their second consecutive loss of the season against the Denver Broncos in Week 8. During the 28-24 loss, the Chiefs got hit with 11 penalties for 105 yards. Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, who caught five receptions for 62 yards against Denver, spoke to reporters after Kansas City fell to second place in the AFC West. “We got a lot of fight,” he said. “You got to take the positives out of this. You can’t dwell on it. They’re a pretty good football team,” Kelce said of the Broncos, a team they crushed 31-10 in Week 1. Getty Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce runs the ball against the Broncos in Week 8. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid faced criticism for his questionable play calls against the Broncos, like sending out a struggling Harrison Butker to kick a 54-yard field goal in the rain on 4th and eight. His mysterious decision to keep left guard Kingsley Suamataia on the bench also left fans perplexed. After the game, Kelce shared a strong message about Reid. Travis Kelce Says It’s Their Job to Make Chiefs Head Coach Andy Reid’s Plays Work While Kelce wants to see the film “and see what the answers are and how we can get better from it,” the 37-year-old made it clear that the fault is in their execution, not Reid’s play calls. Getty Chiefs head coach Andy Reid has the full support from tight end Travis Kelce. “There’s a mentality that whatever Coach Reid calls, you got to find a way to get it into the end zone,” he said. “And that’s the bottom line . That’s the mentality. And from here on out, it’s gotta be how we roll. And we have to execute.” Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is on the same page. “Yeah, obviously penalties, some miscommunications between me and the receivers and running backs and stuff like that,” Mahomes told reporters. “Just in general, the execution wasn’t at a high enough level.” “We made big plays, and we made plays happen against a really good defense. But whenever you’re playing a team like that in the division, you’ve got to execute for the full 60 minutes, and we weren’t able to do that.” As for Sumataia’s benching, Kelce said he loves the guy and is “not sure what the scenario” is there. item.title: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley doesn’t hold back on Philadelphia’s free fall
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Eagles RB Saquon Barkley doesn’t hold back on Philadelphia’s free fall appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles ’ losing streak keeps growing after a loss to the Washington Commander s, and Saquon Barkley is not sugarcoating how it feels. After Philadelphia fell 27-10 on Sunday Night Football , the star running back gave a blunt assessment of where the team stands. “This one sucks. They all suck,” Barkley said, via Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. “The mindset is continue to stay together, but in reality, we’ve got to go back to the little things and lock in our details. Keeps getting us beat.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Saquon Barkley: "This one sucks. They all suck. The mindset is continue to stay together, but in reality, we've got to go back to the little things and lock in our details. Keeps getting us beat. "We've got to lock in, fast." pic.twitter.com/DL1rDJNQcw — Olivia Reiner (@ReinerOlivia) November 2, 2026 Barkley added, “We’ve got to lock in, fast.” The defeat was the Eagles’ sixth straight, dropping them to 2-6 on the season . It started well enough at Northwest Stadium. Jake Elliott opened the scoring with a 40-yard field goal, and Barkley took a direct snap and punched in a 3-yard touchdown run to give Philadelphia a 10-0 lead in the first quarter. The Eagles did not score again. Washington answered with 27 unanswered points, as Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an 8-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the Commanders added four field goals, including a 56-yarder. A 1-yard touchdown run and a two-point conversion with 1:55 left capped the scoring. The win improved Washington to 2-4-1 and marked its first comeback victory of the season. Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown without an interception, while the Commanders’ defense sacked Tanner McKee five times. McKee, filling in for the injured Jalen Hurts, went 23-of-34 for 212 yards with an interception. Barkley, who entered the week dealing with hamstring and back injuries, was held to 30 yards on 13 carries. He added a 24-yard catch out of the backfield. Elijah Mitchell, elevated from the practice squad on Saturday , also got 11 carries. The 29-year-old is not the only Eagle taking accountability during the skid. Last week, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio took the blame after the Dallas Cowboys ran for 204 yards in a 38-21 loss on Monday Night Football. The good news for Philadelphia is that the NFC East remains up for grabs. The New York Giants lead the division at 4-2-1, and the Eagles will host them at Lincoln Financial Field next Sunday. The Philadelphia Eagles ’ losing streak keeps growing after a loss to the Washington Commander s, and Saquon Barkley is not sugarcoating how it feels. After Philadelphia fell 27-10 on Sunday Night Football , the star running back gave a blunt assessment of where the team stands. “This one sucks. They all suck,” Barkley said, via Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. “The mindset is continue to stay together, but in reality, we’ve got to go back to the little things and lock in our details. Keeps getting us beat.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Saquon Barkley: "This one sucks. They all suck. The mindset is continue to stay together, but in reality, we've got to go back to the little things and lock in our details. Keeps getting us beat. "We've got to lock in, fast." pic.twitter.com/DL1rDJNQcw — Olivia Reiner (@ReinerOlivia) November 2, 2026 Barkley added, “We’ve got to lock in, fast.” The defeat was the Eagles’ sixth straight, dropping them to 2-6 on the season . It started well enough at Northwest Stadium. Jake Elliott opened the scoring with a 40-yard field goal, and Barkley took a direct snap and punched in a 3-yard touchdown run to give Philadelphia a 10-0 lead in the first quarter. The Eagles did not score again. Washington answered with 27 unanswered points, as Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an 8-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the Commanders added four field goals, including a 56-yarder. A 1-yard touchdown run and a two-point conversion with 1:55 left capped the scoring. The win improved Washington to 2-4-1 and marked its first comeback victory of the season. Daniels completed 16 of 29 passes for 217 yards and a touchdown without an interception, while the Commanders’ defense sacked Tanner McKee five times. McKee, filling in for the injured Jalen Hurts, went 23-of-34 for 212 yards with an interception. Barkley, who entered the week dealing with hamstring and back injuries, was held to 30 yards on 13 carries. He added a 24-yard catch out of the backfield. Elijah Mitchell, elevated from the practice squad on Saturday , also got 11 carries. The 29-year-old is not the only Eagle taking accountability during the skid. Last week, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio took the blame after the Dallas Cowboys ran for 204 yards in a 38-21 loss on Monday Night Football. The good news for Philadelphia is that the NFC East remains up for grabs. The New York Giants lead the division at 4-2-1, and the Eagles will host them at Lincoln Financial Field next Sunday. If Philadelphia hopes to salvage its season, the turnaround will need to start there. item.title: “He Is Washed Up,” “Not a Top 5 QB Anymore”: NFL Fans Rip Patrick Mahomes After Costly Error Leads to Chiefs’ Loss vs. Broncos
item.description: Aug 28, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) reacts during the second half against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium. © Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Patrick Mahomes is facing the heat after making a costly mistake that cost the Kansas City Chiefs the game in Sunday’s 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. Andy Reid and his team led 24-21. During a third-and-2 with 2:44 left, the three-time Super Bowl champion tried to find space in the pocket to make a pass. Mahomes ran to the right before being sacked by linebacker Alex Singleton , resulting in a 6-yard loss. Harrison Butker then came on for a 54-yard field-goal attempt. However, he missed, and possession changed hands. The Broncos then set up running back Jonah Coleman for a 5-yard rushing TD, which put Sean Payton and his team ahead for good. Fans on social media did not shy away from criticizing Patrick Mahomes for the costly sack. “Patrick Mahomes is not a top 5 QB anymore. He may not be top 10,” one fan commented. “Chiefs about to lose because Patrick Mahomes took an idiotic sack. That brother is washed up,” another fan said. Here are more reactions: With a few seconds left in the game, it looked like the Chiefs (5-2) scored a go-ahead touchdown to win the game. However, Jaylon Moore was flagged for a false start, nullifying the play. On fourth-and-goal, Patrick Mahomes ended up being sacked by defensive tackle Malcolm Roach as time expired. The three-time Super Bowl champion completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards and three TDs. Patrick Mahomes expresses disappointment after Sunday’s loss to the Denver Broncos In the postgame news conference, Patrick Mahomes admitted that the Kansas City Chiefs made a lot of mistakes that cost them the game. “We just made too many mistakes,” Mahomes said. “When you make mistakes, you’re going to lose against good football teams.” The quarterback also vowed to improve despite the loss to the Denver Broncos. “Obviously it’s a big game, I’m not going to hide from that, but now you’re in a dogfight for the division. I was proud of how the guys battled; it wasn’t perfect, but we battled. We’ll learn from it.” The Chiefs are next scheduled to face the New York Jets on Sunday. item.title: ‘Advantage In Every Area’ – Lucas Gabriel Aims To End Magomed Magomedov’s Unbeaten Run At ONE Fight Night 49
item.description: Lucas Gabriel steps into his first main event on martial arts’ grandest stage, and he plans to make the most of the moment. He faces undefeated promotional newcomer Magomed “Muhammad” Magomedov in a lightweight MMA showdown at ONE Fight Night 49 on Prime Video , which goes down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6. Photo Credit: ONE Championship His opponent, however, was never part of the original plan. The Brazilian had spent his camp preparing for former ONE Lightweight MMA World Title challenger Alibeg Rasulov , until an injury forced the Turkish star off the card. Magomedov – a perfect 15-0 in his career – answered on short notice. A swap this close to fight night can tilt a camp off its axis, but Gabriel’s blueprint has stayed intact. Gabriel told onefc.com: “He has a similar style to my previous opponent, so I haven’t had to change much since the fight was switched. I know he’s an undefeated and well-rounded fighter.” View this post on Instagram While the Phuket Fight Club affiliate respects Magomedov’s credentials , he expects the Dagestani to stay true to his roots, and he is ready to meet him there. A Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt with heavy hands to match, Gabriel can end a fight from anywhere, and he has a firm read on how this one unfolds. The 26-year-old said: “He tends to rely more on grappling, which often leaves openings in his stand-up game. I believe I have the advantage in every area. My jiu-jitsu is much better, and I also believe my striking is superior.” Photo Credit: ONE Championship Gabriel sounds certain he is a step ahead wherever this fight goes, and he plans to prove it with a finish. A seventh straight appearance without defeat in the world’s largest martial arts organization is the goal, and he wants it to arrive with an ending the highlight reels will replay. Gabriel, after all, has built an 11-1 record on pressure and power, and he has a clear idea of how the script on fight night will read. He said: “I want to finish the fight, no matter how it happens. Beating an undefeated opponent is always a great thing for your career. I don’t want to leave the decision in the judges’ hands. My goal is to take control and find a way to get the finish.” View this post on Instagram Gabriel Is Coming For The Lightweight Crown Lucas Gabriel believes a statement win in Bangkok would thrust him straight into the ONE Lightweight MMA World Title picture, and the timing could hardly be better. Two-division king Christian “The Warrior” Lee defends the lightweight gold against Tye Ruotolo at The Inner Circle 37 just hours before Gabriel steps into the mecca of Muay Thai. Whoever leaves with the belt, the Phuket-based fighter believes he could be next in line. item.title: Liverpool’s work in progress fizzles out in the face of streetwise champions | Andy Hunter
item.description: Afternoon began with talk of a title bid, but Arsenal looked more and more comfortable as the second half wore on Andoni Iraola had swatted aside any question that veered in the direction of Liverpool’s title credentials during his press conference on Friday with two simple words. “Too early,” he would respond. The Liverpool head coach was dismissive in terms of the stage of the season but, as Arsenal doggedly demonstrated, too early also applies to the development of his team. Arsenal cavorted to the sound of fury at Anfield. At the final whistle Mikel Arteta leapt into the arms of the first-team coach Gabriel Heinze as he celebrated the release of his first win at Liverpool as Arsenal manager, his club’s first league victory at Anfield in 14 years and the champions moving three points clear at the top of the table. His players, tireless in the protection of Kai Havertz’s early winner, lined up to accept the acclaim from a jubilant away section. Anger filled the space around them. Continue reading...

item.title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts? | Andrew Beasley
item.description: Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change. The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away. Continue reading...

item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: Spurs see off Crystal Palace after Mateta’s early red to pile pressure on Sage
item.description: Fortune is not favouring Pierre Sage. Just when the Crystal Palace manager needed a positive result, Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card condemned his side to a third straight defeat in the league, leaving their manager’s position hanging by a thread. Goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke ensured that Tottenham recorded a third successive victory for the first time in 616 days as they moved into the top half of the table. To put that into context, Spurs have had three full-time managers since then, so it was no wonder that Roberto De Zerbi looked so pleased at full time. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester United’s capitulation at Chelsea paints picture of a club that barely exists | Barney Ronay
item.description: Michael Carrick is now a little more pre-doomed, pre-sacked, but is miles away from being the actual story On and on and on. And then on just a little bit more it would seem. Manchester United: always crashing in the same Carrick. The obvious question after this 2-0 defeat against Chelsea is how much longer United will continue to lose games under the current manager, as opposed to losing games under the next one. But it is also a mark of the dysfunction of this club, its ambient levels of sadness, that this matters so little. Continue reading...

item.title: Sakamoto sparks Coventry win to keep 10-man Sunderland rock-bottom
item.description: Coventry climbed out of the relegation zone with a win that leaves Sunderland rooted to the bottom of the Premier League. Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s first Premier League goal put Coventry ahead 17 minutes in, Taiwo Awoniyi’s first league goal for the home side doubled the lead eight minutes before the break and Jack Rudoni sealed victory early in the second half. Sunderland were offered a little hope when Enzo Le Fée sent Carl Rushworth the wrong way from the penalty spot in the 67th minute, but they grew increasingly frustrated and finished the match with 10 men when Omar Alderete was shown a second yellow card in stoppage time. Continue reading...

item.title: Evanilson profits from costly Trafford blunder as Bournemouth punish Leeds
item.description: Accidents will happen. They also have consequences. Leeds were playing well, certainly better than Bournemouth for the first 30 minutes until James Trafford committed his grievous error. The goalkeeper made a horrible mess of a pass to an unwitting Ao Tanaka. In stole Justin Kluivert to set up Evanilson for a fifth goal in six matches. Where Leeds’s confidence sagged, Evanilson continued to find the best form of his time on the south coast. “I just met him and told him you are a real No 9,” Marco Rose said of the Brazilian who was full of intelligent movement. “He has to reward himself with goals and that is what he is doing.” Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I’m not here to be liked’: Glasner defiant as Brentford capitalise on Forest woes
item.description: For Oliver Glasner and Nottingham Forest, the future starts now. His post-match press conference lasted 14 frustrated minutes in which, repeatedly banging the desk, he blamed himself for compromising his principles and told players that if they didn’t “buy in” they could “leave”. “For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation that the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.” Continue reading...

item.title: How can playing for Manchester City fit into Marc Guéhi’s moral universe? | Barney Ronay
item.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier League I felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. I realised I didn’t want to be with all these people. Somebody came at me, a huge individual in silver and blue. I fell at his feet and grabbed one shoe. I started untying the lace. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry. Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. This is instead a condensed quote from the mind of Gary Harkness, existentially curious college running-back and the narrator of Don DeLillo’s great American football novel End Zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Grealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo
item.description: After being dropped for ‘a breach of club discipline’, the winger must face the same questions about respect and self-awareness For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man. That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “ a breach of club discipline ”. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...
